articles.title: ESPN Cameraman Under Fire For His Zooming In Sunday Night
articles.summary: The ESPN cameraman went viral.
articles.body:
Ole Miss football held off Louisville, 41-38, in an exciting Week 1 college football game on Sunday evening.

The Rebels, who lost head coach Lane Kiffin to LSU during the offseason, are hoping to contend for a College Football Playoff berth in their new era. Ole Miss got off to a good start on Sunday night, taking down a good Louisville team. The Rebels opened the season with an impressive victory, starting off the year at 1-0, while the Cardinals dropped to a disappointing 0-1.

Late in the game, during a tense moment, ESPN's cameraman found a stressed-out Ole Miss fan in the crowd. The Ole Miss fan quickly went viral on X, formerly known as Twitter, on Sunday evening.

The cameraman decided to zoom in on the young Ole Miss Rebels fan on Sunday night, catching fire on social media.

"The cameraman at the Ole Miss – Louisville game understood the assignment. Bro zoomed in. I'M CRYING 😂," one fan wrote.

"Understood the assignment is funny until you remember somebody's family is watching the feed," one fan joked.

"The man deserves a raise and a producer credit," one fan added.

"She should've been cast in The Odyssey," one fan added.

Ole Miss has a lot of support, but it was one fan in particular who shined on Sunday evening, as many took to social media to react to the viral moment between the Rebels and the Cardinals.

Week 1 of the 2026 college football regular season will continue on Labor Day evening, before we turn the page toward Week 2. The second week of the 2026 college football season will of course be highlighted by Ohio State's road trip to Texas, in a potential College Football Playoff national title game preview.

This story was originally published by The Spun on Sep 7, 2026, where it first appeared in the College Football section. Add The Spun as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani Returns To Dodgers Lineup As DH, Pitching Again 'Not Dead'
articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani was back in the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup as designated hitter on Monday night after a four-day break to deal with lingering left knee, right biceps and neck soreness.
articles.body: Shohei Ohtani was back in the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup as designated hitter on Monday night after a four-day break to deal with lingering left knee, right biceps and neck soreness. He was in his usual leadoff spot for the series opener against the Cincinnati Reds. "Hopefully, we don’t see that wincing we saw a handful of nights ago," manager Dave Roberts said before the game, referring to Ohtani appearing physically compromised at the plate before his break. "I don’t want to say it’s day-to-day, but I am very curious to see how he comes out of tonight to then make the decision for tomorrow and ensuing days," Roberts said. The NL West-leading Dodgers won all four games during Ohtani’s absence, including a sweep of the Washington Nationals. Even with Ohtani’s return as a hitter, it appears increasingly unlikely that the two-way superstar will pitch again this season. He hasn’t pitched in a game since July 3 and he hasn’t thrown since a bullpen session at Detroit on Aug. 28. "We’ve put a pin in throwing," Roberts said, "and just having him focus on the hitting, the running, keeping his legs good and doing whatever it takes to help us win." Asked to define "put a pin in throwing," Roberts said "it’s not dead but we have no timetable for when he’s going to pick up a baseball." Why not just say Ohtani won't pitch again? "I'm choosing not to say it's dead," Roberts said. Ohtani's thoughts remain private since he hasn't spoken to the media since Aug. 17. Roberts described Ohtani as "happy" to be back in the lineup while being "completely fine" about tabling any pitching plans for now. By taking pitching off Ohtani's plate, the Dodgers hope the four-time MVP will lock in on hitting and get back on track after not appearing to be himself at the plate. Ohtani is hitting .279 with 30 homers and 80 RBIs this season. Since the All-Star break, however, he’s batting .250 with eight homers and 22 RBIs in 41 games. "Yes, he loves pitching, loves being a two-way player," Roberts said, "but right now it just doesn’t make any sense. It’s more of what’s best for the team, number one, and 1A, what’s best for him." Utility player Tommy Edman took Ohtani's place as the leadoff hitter for four games. He went 7 for 17 with a .412 average, one home run, four RBIs and five runs scored. He was scheduled to start at second and bat third on Monday. Asked why he doesn't move Ohtani out of the leadoff spot, Roberts replied, "I think he’s our best hitter. I think the best player should have the most latitude. Is it forever? I don’t know. Is it until the end of the season? I don’t know yet." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Gary McCoy: What drives road racer after second big crash in 13 months?
articles.summary: After he injured his back in his second big crash in 13 months, Gary McCoy speaks to the BBC Bikes podcast about his recovery and drive to return to racing.
articles.body:
When Gary McCoy slid off his bike at the Isle of Man TT in June, he had two seconds to process what was about to happen.

"'Oh no, not again.' I knew what was coming," he recalled.

The Northern Ireland road racer ended up in hospital with five broken vertebrae in his back, one of which was crushed, and a broken shoulder blade.

Just 13 months earlier, McCoy had another big crash at the North West 200 which left him with serious injuries.

On that occasion, a following rider crashed into McCoy from behind approaching Mill Road roundabout and he was left with a bleed in the brain, a punctured lung and 22 broken bones.

Yet, despite an extensive list of injuries from the two accidents, McCoy plans to get back on the bike and hit the roads again next year.

Speaking to the BBC Bikes podcast , McCoy says he was in "disbelief" after his accident at the Isle of Man TT, and says he was "very, very lucky", but the thought of competing again is not only driving on his recovery, but also his drive to get back to work.

"Whenever you want something bad enough you sort of look by it all, and it keeps you going forward," he said.

"But motorbikes is driving me on, motorbikes is driving me on to get fitter and get better, get back to work, get back to racing.

"If you didn't know motorbikes, you would have no drive. I don't think so. I don't think so. It's driving me on at the minute and long may it last."

McCoy 'awaiting results of scan on vertebrae injuries'

McCoy grew up watching road racing right across Ireland with his family, but it wasn't until he was 21 that he started competing.

He made his North West 200 debut in 2022, when he was the best newcomer, and had several top 10 finishes at the international road race.

After he recovered from his 2025 North West 200 accident, the 27-year-old was primed to make his TT debut for the family-run MadBros team in June, and things had started well.

McCoy had shown impressive form in qualifying as a newcomer but an accident in damp conditions in the opening Supersport race brought his TT debut to a sudden halt.

"Prior to the crash, everything was absolutely amazing. It was the best thing I've ever done," McCoy added.

"It's all I've ever wanted to do from when I was three or four years of age.

"So, after twenty seven years of wanting to do it, and finally getting to do it, it was unbelievable."

On his crash, which happened at the Kerrowmoar section of the 37.73-mile circuit on the third lap of the race, McCoy was still looking at the positives.

"We were just caught out in the damp patch and chatting to a few others, even Michael Dunlap said to the boys he had a wee moment down through it, and Paul Jordan had a wee moment through it.

"A few top boys were having moments, you know, so it's just unfortunate that a newcomer had to get caught out and that is what it is."

McCoy has two young children and a wife, Leana, and admits that road racing is "a very selfish sport".

He admits Leana would be happy if he stayed away from the bike and there is a lot of pressure on her, but she is supportive of him racing.

McCoy says he moved back in with his mum and dad for three months after his 2025 crash as Leana was dealing with a newborn, and says she is a "strong woman".

"You just think it is never going to be you in that situation," McCoy said about the dangers of the sport."

"All I wanted to do was race motorbikes and I'm doing it.

"I can't really explain it any more than that. It's all I've ever wanted. So I'm doing it and I'm not going to give up on it."

McCoy says his full focus is on returning to the North West 200 and Isle of Man TT, where he wants to be progressing.

For the TT in particular, the Cookstown rider said he "can't describe the feeling" of getting ready to set off down Bray Hill for the opening laps.

"Until you actually experience it and until you actually experience it and do the Isle of Man TT, you can't really explain what it means or how it feels.

Listen to the BBC Bikes podcast with Gary McCoy and Stephen Watson on BBC Sounds.

articles.title: US Open: Zheng in 5-0 comeback; Gauff, Rybakina, Zverev also in quarters
articles.summary: Zheng Qinwen beats Iga Swiatek; Coco Gauff, Elena Rybakina also reach quarterfinals. Alexander Zverev through in men’s.
articles.body:
Home favourite Coco Gauff and world number two Elena Rybakina sailed into the US Open quarterfinals, while China’s Zheng Qinwen mounted another extraordinary fightback to upset six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek.

Top seed Alexander Zverev beat Italian ⁠Luciano Darderi 6-2, 6-2, 7-6(3) at Arthur Ashe Stadium. The German was surprised to finish before midnight after coming through a couple of five-setters earlier in the tournament.

“I think after 10 hours on court, I just maybe found my rhythm a little bit better, which is helpful because the first two matches ⁠were really not [at a] great level,” Zverev said after his win late on Monday.

“I think I’m going in the right direction, moving forward in the right direction.”

Zverev, who is bidding for a second Grand Slam title after winning the French Open in June, avenged his defeat by Darderi at the Italian Open in Rome earlier this year.

Fourth seed Gauff outclassed compatriot Iva Jovic 6-1, 6-4 to set up a clash with French Open champion Mirra Andreeva for a place in the semis.

“Mirra is someone that I always have ‌tough matches with,” Gauff told reporters. “She’s obviously in a different mindset now at the top of the game coming off of a Grand Slam win … it’s going to be a really athletic, tough match.”

Gauff is the sixth American player into the quarters, joining Jessica Pegula, Emma Navarro, Frances Tiafoe, Alex Michelsen and Ben Shelton.

Rybakina continued her quest for a third major title with a 6-1, 6-4 win over former US Open champion Naomi Osaka, who was hampered by an Achilles tendon injury that had flared up in the previous round.

The victory leaves second seed Rybakina one win away from becoming world number one for the first time, with Olympic champion Zheng awaiting her in the quarters.

The win was another encouraging sign for ⁠Rybakina, who had arrived in New York with questions over her fitness after retiring from the Cincinnati Open in the ⁠build-up to the tournament.

“Preparation wasn’t that great,” she told reporters. “It’s an amazing progress. I’m really glad how everything worked out.”

Zheng has become something of an escape artist at Flushing Meadows.

After coming back from a 0-5 deficit in the deciding set against third-round foe Madison Keys, she let the first five games slip through her fingers in 20 minutes against 2022 ⁠champion Swiatek.

However, she clawed her way back into the match and collapsed to the court with her face in her hands after sealing the win on the fourth match point.

Zheng is the first qualifier since Emma Raducanu in 2021 ⁠to reach the quarterfinals of the women’s draw, as she battles back from a chronic elbow ⁠injury.

Andreeva’s entertaining match against Anastasia Potapova ended on a sour note as the Austrian went down injured in the final game.

Potapova valiantly retook the court but could not prevent the inevitable as Andreeva sealed the 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 win with a backhand strike before going across the net to hug her opponent.

The evening session in the men’s draw was not short on drama.

At ‌Louis Armstrong Stadium, Karen Khachanov fought back to claim a 7-5, 4-6, 6-7(6), 6-1, 6-4 win over 20-year-old American Learner Tien, while on the Grandstand court, Botic van de Zandschulp emerged victorious after a five-hour marathon against Arthur Gea.

The 21-year-old Gea had been one point away from becoming the first lucky loser ‌in ‌Grand Slam history to reach the quarterfinals, before his Dutch opponent engineered a 3-6, 6-7(0), 7-6(7), 7-6(3), 6-4 comeback win.

Earlier on Monday, Belgium’s Alexander Blockx dispatched Argentine 24th seed Francisco Cerundolo 6-3, 4-6, 7-5, 7-5 to reach his first Grand Slam quarterfinal.

articles.title: Dacia Spring 2027: cambia al completo, deja de ser 'chino' y te sorprenderá por su precio
articles.standfirst: Dacia 'democratizó' los eléctricos con el Spring, que ahora estrena una segunda generación fabricada en Europa, con 250 km de autonomía y una tarifa que será uno de sus grandes atractivos.
articles.summary: Dacia 'democratizó' los eléctricos con el Spring, que ahora estrena una segunda generación fabricada en Europa, con 250 km de autonomía y una tarifa por debajo de los 20.000 euros. Así es este nuevo utilitario.
articles.body: La electrificación empezó a construirse por el tejado. Modelos de gran tamaño, con carrocerías poco aerodinámicas y baterías de gran tamaño empezaron a copar el mercado. Cierto es que sus datos de rendimiento y, sobre todo, de rango permitían incluso pensar en largos viajes sin necesidad de vivir agobiados. En cambio, su principal desventaja fue, claramente, la económica ya que sus desorbitados precios (con los que resultaba más sencillo diluir el coste de la batería) provocaron que únicamente fueran accesibles para las clases más altas. Una condición que se fue convirtió en una gran barrera de cara a las propias matriculaciones. Pero como en otras muchas ocasiones, Dacia decidió ir a contracorriente ya que se convirtió en una de las primeras en escuchar realmente al usuario, que buscaba coches eléctricos asequibles y pequeños. Así, en 2021 apareció el Spring. Un coche sin grandes pretensiones técnicas, con unas prestaciones modestas y una autonomía contenida, pero con algo que hasta ese momento no se había dado: un precio realmente accesible. La fórmula habla por sí misma ya que desde ese momento se han superado las 210.000 unidades vendidas en más de cuarenta países, permitiendo a muchos compradores entrar de lleno en la electrificación. Ahora, un lustro después, Dacia mueve ficha y lo hace de manera mucho más agresiva que con el par de actualizaciones sufridas anteriormente por el modelo, ya que esta segunda entrega conserva el nombre y poco más. Un vehículo que hemos podido conocer en persona antes de su desembarco comercial, dejándonos una primera impresión muy sorprendente, pues ya no parece un coche que necesite paliar una necesidad, sino un urbano eléctrico concebido desde el inicio para Europa y para enfrentarse a una competencia que cada vez está más concienciada con ofrecer modelos por debajo de los 20.000 euros. En este caso, lo más representativo del coche no solo es el diseño (en el que ahora entraremos), sino sus ‘tripas’, pues ahora utiliza la nueva plataforma eléctrica RGEV small de Renault Group (la misma que la del Twingo) que ha sido desarrollada en menos de dos años. Además, abandona la producción china del anterior Spring (se ensamblaba en Shiyan) para fabricarse en Novo Mesto, Eslovenia. Una fabricación europea que tiene igualmente una lectura comercial importante, sobre todo en países como España, donde ayudas como el Plan Auto+ están supeditadas a varios condicionantes, entre ellos, la fabricación en el Viejo Continente, mientras que en un espectro más amplio, este coche ahora dejaría de estar sujeto a posibles aranceles. El uso de esta nueva plataforma le dota de un sinfín de ventajas. La primera, el cambio de proporciones, que se nota nada más verlo. El nuevo Spring alcanza ahora los 3,85 metros de longitud y 1,74 metros de anchura, lo que supone crecer 15 y nada menos que 18 centímetros, respectivamente. Un crecimiento que suprime de golpe y porrazo esa sensación de cuadriciclo que transmitía la generación ya saliente. Ello no impide que siga siendo un coche pequeño, manejable y urbano, pero transmite una mayor sensación de solidez visual. El capó es corto y alto, los extremos de la carrocería son bastante verticales y los pasos de rueda adquieren más volumen. El frontal y la zaga están terminados en un plástico negro “tintado en masa”, como lo denomina la propia marca, y que está pensado para soportar mejor los pequeños roces urbanos. Un detalle, este último, muy al estilo Dacia, es decir, que responda a los criterios de coste y durabilidad. Incluso otros detalles como los de la propia iluminación emplean menos componentes gracias al uso de superficies reflectantes en lugar de multiplicar los módulos LED. Esto se traslada igualmente a elementos como las llantas, que siendo de 16” no son de aleación sino de acero (es decir, con tapacubos), o la paleta de colores, que ha suprimido los tonos extravagantes como el naranja o el beige para dejar solo cuatro opciones más 'metropolitanas' entre las que la más destaca es este azul grisáceo denominado Ágave. El aumento de sus cotas exteriores tiene repercusión, lógicamente, en el interior. Porque ahora los asientos no solo resultan más confortables sino que ganan anchura, suprimiendo por ejemplo que conductor y pasajero se toquen entre sí con los brazos o permitiendo colocar sillitas infantiles en su zona trasera con mayor comodidad. Entre algunas de las novedades están la regulación del asiento en altura, así como la del volante, que ahora puede ajustarse tanto verticalmente como en profundidad. Detrás, mantenemos las cuatro plazas, pero ahora, como decimos, son mucho más habitables, tanto por hueco para las rodillas como para la cabeza o la anchura. En cambio, en comparación con el Twingo, no cuentan con desplazamiento longitudinal. De esta forma, el maletero cubica siempre la misma capacidad, que Dacia cifra en 337 litros (29 más que antes), contando hasta la bandeja, pero también con el doble fondo que resulta muy práctico para dejar enseres más valiosos. Porque los cables de carga se podrán colocar en un pequeño compartimento delantero de 18 litros que, eso sí, es opcional. En caso de requerir más volumen, siempre se pueden abatir los respaldos posteriores en una proporción 50/50 y gozar de los 1.283 litros disponibles. Como en otros Dacia, cuenta con los conocidos puntos de fijación YouClip para instalar portavasos, linternas, bolsas u otros accesorios. El salpicadero también da un salto evolutivo importante tanto en presencia como en uso de materiales, que si bien siguen abundando los plásticos duros, los ajustes son mucho más sólidos. Igualmente, se mantienen los comandos físicos tanto en el volante como para el climatizador, con los típicos diales giratorios del grupo Renault y que desde aquí agradecemos. Un detalle importante es que todos los acabados incorporan de serie la instrumentación digital de 7 pulgadas, mientras que el Journey, el más alto y que nosotros vimos, añade un sistema Media Nav Live con pantalla táctil de 10,1 pulgadas, Apple CarPlay y Android Auto inalámbricos, navegación conectada durante ocho años y servicios remotos. Porque para el nivel Expression, emplea una solución mucho más barata y bastante inteligente: Media Control, que utiliza el teléfono móvil como pantalla principal mediante un soporte integrado y una aplicación específica. Al emplear la misma plataforma que el Renault Twingo E-Tech, era de recibo que se replicara su versión mecánica. Y sí, hablamos en singular porque ahora el Spring deja de poder escogerse con dos versiones para dejar únicamente una de 80 CV que reciba la energía de una batería LFP de 27,5 kWh. Pude que a muchos les chirríe esta decisión, más cuando la versión de 100 CV convertía al Spring en un auténtico cohete con ruedas. Sin embargo, las prestaciones siguen siendo más que correctas para un coche uso urbano: 12,1 segundos para pasar de 0 a 100 km/h y 130 km/h de velocidad punta. Más aún cuando los datos que maneja Dacia de los conductores de su Spring son determinantes: la mayoría recorre una media de 34 kilómetros diarios a una velocidad media de 34 km/h y el 75% recarga habitualmente en casa. Una variable esta última también importante porque el nuevo Spring lleva embarcado un cargador en corriente alterna de 6,6 kW. En caso de requerir una de 11 kW y, sobre todo, una en continua de 50 kW habrá que pasar por caja para sumar el Pack Charge con el que también se suma la función bidireccional V2L. Hace cinco años, Dacia entendió la necesidad de ofrecer un coche pequeño, con un rango de autonomía ideal para el día a día y con una sencillez general que evitara cualquier tipo de conflicto para el comprador. Hoy el panorama es bien diferente, pues la competencia ha emergido llegando con argumentos similares a los de aquel primer Spring. Por eso ahora la firma franco-rumana ha sabido evolucionar el concepto y aprovechar su simbiosis con Renault para lanzar un modelo mucho más maduro. Todo ello sin variar la que es su gran baza: el precio. Si bien Dacia todavía no ha comunicado la tarifa española exacta, sí ha confirmado algo mucho más importante: todas las versiones del nuevo Spring costarán menos de 20.000 euros antes de ayudas públicas. De hecho, la gama partirá por debajo de los 18.000 euros en el acabado Expression, lo que con ayudas y descuentos podría situarle por debajo de los 13.000 euros (un Twingo arranca por debajo de los 14.000 euros). El problema para Dacia es que ese listón ya no resulta tan extraordinario como hace cinco años sobre todo teniendo en cuenta que hay opciones como el BYD Dolphin Surf, el Citroën C3, el Hyundai INSTER o el propio Twingo, pero ser el pionero puede ser un punto muy a favor.

articles.title: In 2018, Vidarsa K Vinod walked into a college NCC trial simply to experience holding a rifle; eight years, borrowed equipment and a family loan later, she is going to the Asian Games
articles.summary: More sports News: When Vidarsa K Vinod walked into an NCC shooting trial at her college in Kozhikode in 2018, she wanted to experience what it felt like to hold a rifle.
articles.body: When Vidarsa K Vinod walked into an NCC shooting trial at her college in Kozhikode in 2018, she wanted to experience what it felt like to hold a rifle. Eight years later, that casual decision has taken the Kerala shooter to the biggest stage of her career. Vinod is set to make her Asian Games debut in Aichi-Nagoya, representing India in the women’s 10m air rifle and 50m rifle 3 positions events.Her journey, however, was anything but straightforward. For years, she trained without owning the equipment needed to compete seriously. She relied on NCC and borrowed rifles, dealt with the financial demands of shooting and even came close to quitting before finally breaking through.She entered shooting almost by chanceAccording to The Indian Express, Vinod had no formal shooting training when she appeared for the NCC trial in 2018. She performed well enough to make the NCC team and soon progressed to the Kerala state team. A year later, she became the aggregate champion at the Kerala State Shooting Championship. But becoming a serious shooter required something she did not have: her own rifle.Competitive shooting is an expensive sport, with the cost of a rifle coming before expenses such as jackets and ammunition. For Vinod, that financial barrier remained a constant problem. The Covid-19 pandemic made matters worse, bringing her training to a halt.For nearly a year, she stayed away from the range and practised yoga and exercises at home. Even before that, she had been relying on borrowed or NCC equipment. Yet despite not owning a rifle, she rose to No. 1 in Kerala, according to The Indian Express.A question changed her careerThe turning point came through another shooter, Manu S Ravi, who later became her husband. After the pandemic, he asked her a simple question: why did she not own a rifle? For Vinod, the answer was obvious- she could not afford one.But the question forced her to reconsider how seriously she wanted to pursue shooting. According to India Today, Vinod discussed the matter with her parents, and in 2021 her family took a loan to buy her first rifle.The investment eventually began to pay off. With Manu’s encouragement and training under coach Manoj Kumar, her performances improved and she won her first national medal in 2022.From Kerala to DelhiVinod moved to New Delhi to train at the Dr Karni Singh Shooting Range, entering a more demanding training environment. It meant living alone in an unfamiliar city while managing cooking, household responsibilities and intensive training sessions.In early 2024, after a series of near-misses and mounting financial strain, Vinod came close to walking away from shooting. She felt that her family, husband and coach had already sacrificed too much for her career. But they continued to back her, even when she had begun to doubt herself.A rifle that was never meant to be hersThere was another unusual twist in her equipment story. Vinod was struggling with the weight of her rifle, and coach Manoj Kumar suggested that she try a lighter model he had imported for his daughter. As per reports, Kumar's daughter ultimately chose to focus on studies, so he allowed Vinod to test the rifle.She initially refused because the rifle had been bought for his daughter. After trying it for a few days, however, Kumar told her to keep it. That lightweight rifle is now the one Vinod will carry into the Asian Games.Kumar told The Indian Express that Vinod was quick to learn and willing to accept the technical changes he introduced. Their association has continued for several years and has become an important part of her development as a shooter.From her first international medal to the Asian GamesThe breakthrough at the international level came in 2025. Vinod represented India at the Asian Shooting Championships in Kazakhstan and won a silver medal in the team event, according to The Times of India. Since then, she has competed at three ISSF World Cups, two Asian Championships and a World Championship. She also finished sixth at a recent World Cup. Her maiden international medal at the 2025 Asian Shooting Championship helped pave the way for her selection for the Asian Games squad.Now, the woman who once borrowed rifles to continue competing is preparing to take aim for India at the Asian Games. But Vinod is not setting herself a medal target. Speaking to The Times of India, she said her coach's advice has been to focus on experiencing and learning rather than chasing the podium. The emphasis, she said, is on preparing for a longer period rather than treating the Asian Games as a single defining competition. In 2018, she had walked into an NCC trial simply to hold a rifle. articles.title: Leal, Goñi, Salazar…, París define la lista de España para el Mundial
articles.standfirst: La lista de convocados para Doha se hará oficial el próximo 24 de septiembre y entre Madrid y el segundo Major se van a dejar cerradas ambas convocatorias
articles.summary: La lista de convocados para Doha se hará oficial el próximo 24 de septiembre y entre Madrid y el segundo Major se van a dejar cerradas ambas convocatorias
articles.body: Al Mundial se viaja vía París. La Selección Española de pádel tiene casi todo definido para cerrar la lista de convocados de cara a la cita de noviembre y el segundo Major de la temporada Premier Padel va a acabar por despejar las pocas dudas que quedan de cara a quiénes serán los convocados. Y es que según ha podido conocer MARCA Pádel la convocatoria para el Mundial por selección de noviembre está clara y solo hay dos dudas por resolver que “dependen en gran parte de Madrid y París” según comentan extraoficialmente fuentes cercanas … Con varios nombres claros por rendimiento actual, solidez y experiencia con la Selección, el torneo de Roland Garros acabará por conformar la alineación que se hará oficial el próximo jueves 24 de septiembre en Madrid mediante una rueda de prensa por parte de los seleccionadores Juanjo Gutierrez y Carolina Navarro. Es el combinado masculino el que más se juega en el arranque de septiembre. Con Madrid ya consumido y varios batacazos de por medio de algunos de los aspirantes, el torneo de París se antoja clave para despejar las incógnitas que quedan. Arturo Coello, Ale Galán, Juan Lebrón, Mike Yanguas, Paquito Navarro, Coki Nieto conforman el sexteto fijo de la lista de Juanjo Gutiérrez al que deberán sumarse dos nombres más. Y con tres jugadores de revés y otros tantos de drive, solo queda un espacio por lado por cubrir. Jon Sanz, zurdo y agresivo, es el mejor posicionado para cubrir la cuarta posición desde el drive. Su experiencia ya en la parte alta del ranking parece una baza que jugaría además a su favor, pero un buen desempeño de Fran Guerrero en París podría convencer al seleccionador para apostar por un perfil regular y en claro ascenso como el del malagueño. Una situación más complicada incluso vive la última plaza en el revés. Con Aimar Goñi como el gran tapado tal y como publicó este periódico el pasado mes de mayo, la excelsa versión de Javi Leal en los últimos meses no ha pasado desapercibida en la secretaría técnica española. “En Madrid se cruzan”, solo te digo eso. Fue la respuesta clara de la delegación española a MARCA al preguntar por los nombres de Goñi y Leal y que no acabarían viéndose las caras dejando todo en el aire para una resolución inminente estos días en París donde no se verían las caras salvo que ambos, junto a Alonso y Guerrero, sus compañeros, llegaran ala final. Con menos opciones, ya por detrás, aparecen Momo González y Javi Garrido. El primero, un fijo de la Selección los últimos años, no ha acabado de encontrar la regularidad que le caracteriza y a pesar de haber cuajado grandes actuaciones como las semifinales en Roma, no está entre los favoritos. Una situación similar a la de ‘El Khalifa’ que acumula varios resultados seguidos desde junio que le han hecho perder enteros. Una convocatoria que también parece prácticamente cerrada es la del combinado femenino y donde todo hace apuntar a que Carolina Navarro solo albergaría dudas en dos posibles plazas para la expedición española siendo las primeras posiciones del ranking femenino casi un monopolio de españolas. Con Gemma Triay, Paula Josemaría, Bea González, Claudia Fernández, Ariana Sánchez y Andrea Ustero fuera de toda duda, son dos nombres por posición los que desde el entorno de la Selección manejan con hermetismo sin dar demasiadas pistas. Martina Calvo o Tamara Icardo para el revés y Marta Ortega o Alejandra Salazar para ser el cuarto drive. Para el revés, la seleccionadora debe elegir entre el despunte del ‘Huracán Martina’ en el último año y su irrupción y el regreso de la mejor versión de una Icardo que ya fue de hecho campeona en la edición de 2022 con España. Para el drive, Ortega es un seguro de fiabilidad, fija en las convocatorias con España y con un nivel alto todo el año no habiéndose bajado en ningún momento de los cuartos de final mientras que Salazar, ya en el ocaso de su carrera, aspira a su última cita mundialista por la compatibilidad de sus características, la fuerza de su nombre y la vigencia del nivel en pista. Los objetivos para Doha están claros: revalidar el título femenino y recuperar el trono masculino tras dos ediciones. Y París decidirá quiénes son los y las elegidas de España.

articles.title: India’s para archers shine with twin golds, silver at World Archery Para Series
articles.summary: More sports News: India’s para archers enjoyed a strong penultimate day at the World Archery Para Series Stage III, with the men’s recurve and compound teams winning go.
articles.body: India’s para archers enjoyed a strong penultimate day at the World Archery Para Series Stage III, with the men’s recurve and compound teams winning gold while the women’s recurve team secured silver.In the men’s compound team final, reigning world champion Toman Kumar and Shyam Sunder Swami defeated Iraq’s Abbas Kadhim and Anwer Aldawod 152-139 to claim the top prize.The recurve team of double Paralympic medallist Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi also finished on the highest step of the podium after beating Slovakia’s David Ivan and Denis Ivan 6-2.India’s women’s recurve team of Bhawna and Pooja, meanwhile, had to settle for silver after China won the final 6-0. The country also narrowly missed another medal in the women’s compound event, with Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag losing the bronze-medal playoff to China.Toman and Swami deliver compound goldToman and Swami overcame a sluggish beginning to take control of the men’s compound final.The Indian pair managed only an 8 in the opening end but quickly raised their level. Their accuracy improved over the next 12 arrows, during which they dropped just five points.That consistency allowed the Indians to build a substantial advantage over their Iraqi opponents. They maintained their scoring pressure through the remainder of the contest to complete a convincing victory and secure the gold medal.Harvinder leads recurve fightbackHarvinder and Sundi had to recover from an early setback before securing India’s second men’s team gold of the day.The Slovakian pair took the opening set 37-34 after India managed a 7 without finding a 10. The Indians responded immediately, producing stronger scores in the following sets.Harvinder, who won bronze at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics before becoming the first Indian archer to win Paralympic gold at Paris 2024, played a key role in India's recovery.India moved ahead 4-2 after winning the third set 38-34, with the pair producing three 10s. They then held their nerve in the fourth set, winning it 35-31 to complete the 6-2 victory.Bhawna and Pooja take silverBhawna and Pooja could not match China in the women’s recurve final, losing 0-6.China took the opening set 34-23 after India struggled with scores of 4, 5 and 6. The Indians improved in the second set, shooting three 8s and a 9, but still lost 33-35.The third set remained tight at 30-31, but India again struggled for consistency and failed to register a single 10 across the entire final.China did not produce its most clinical performance either, but India's inconsistent arrow placement allowed the Chinese pair to retain their advantage and secure gold.Sheetal and Payal miss bronzeSheetal Devi and Payal Nag were also left without a medal after China’s Wang Huiting and Gao Fangxia won the women’s compound bronze-medal playoff.The Indian pair found it difficult to maintain their scoring level across the 16-arrow contest. Their strongest spell came in the second end, when they trailed by just one point at 73-74.However, a poor third end allowed China to open up a decisive gap. India could not recover from there and eventually had to settle for fourth place.With two golds and a silver on the penultimate day, India remain in contention for a strong finish at the World Archery Para Series Stage III.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Un Desafío de aventureros jubilados: "Nunca imaginamos hacer deporte extremo a nuestra edad"
articles.standfirst: Rafa, Pablo y José reflexionan tras hacer un rápel espectacular de 150 metros sobre sus vivencias en el Desafío Santalucia
articles.summary: Rafa, Pablo y José reflexionan tras hacer un rápel espectacular de 150 metros sobre sus vivencias en el Desafío Santalucia
articles.body: Vietnam tiene rincones mágicos y uno de los más especiales del planeta está en el centro del país, donde adentrarse en sus maravillosas cuevas y hacer un rápel de 150 metros puede convertirse en una de las experiencias más increíbles de la vida como les ha pasado a los expedicionarios del Desafío Santalucia. Pablo San José (71 años), José Puch (70) y Rafa Collado (68) son tres de los cinco expedicionarios y después de completar su particular gesta mantienen en el campamento una entretenida tertulia sobre lo vivido en el Parque Nacional Phong Nha-Ke Bang, el paraíso de la espeleología. "Para mí es un regalo porque aunque llevo en la montaña desde los 14 años y he rapelado, lo que hemos vivido aquí me ha parecido maravilloso y único", afirma el madrileño José Puch. El valenciano Rafa Collado lleva la aventura en sus venas y ya son muchos viajes a sus espaldas por todos los rincones del mundo con su cámara fotográfica como compañía. "Soy aventurero y desde el Covid mucho más, pero nunca imaginé que un día estaría como hoy rapelando en estas cuevas increíbles de Vietnam. Estaba muy intranquilo, tengo que reconocerlo, pero una vez que te sientes seguro lo he disfrutado a lo grande". "Hay mucha gente que tiene nuestra edad y no se plantea un Desafío como el nuestro. Yo creo que es el momento de vivir momentos únicos tanto desde el punto de vista intelectual como del físico", nos cuenta Pablo San José, otro de los componentes del quinteto de Seniors que participan en el Desafío Santalucia Vietnam 2026. "Jubilarse es maravilloso porque tienes todo el tiempo para ti. Soy dueño de mi tiempo", comenta José mientras Pablo recuerda que "la vida siempre te sorprende y yo soy el primer sorprendido con todo lo que estoy viviendo en estos días de duras etapas de bici, trekking y rápel". Rafa se muestra expectante ante la recta final de este Desafío que discurrirá entre cuevas: "Será una nueva experiencia en esta parte de Vietnam que no conocía. Desde que me jubilé decidí vivir y lo estoy haciendo más que nunca".

articles.title: Dylan Larkin, Connor Hellebuyck & Other Trades That Could Still Happen Before 2026 NHL Training Camp
articles.summary: Training camps for the NHL's 2026-27 season will open on Sept. 16 and 17. As general managers of the 32 clubs evaluate their rosters for the coming season, they could turn to the trade market to address any glaring weaknesses.
articles.body:
Training camps for the NHL's 2026-27 season will open on Sept. 16 and 17. As general managers of the 32 clubs evaluate their rosters for the coming season, they could turn to the trade market to address any glaring weaknesses.

Apart from a flurry of activity from June 16 to July 2 , the trade market was quiet for most of the summer. It wasn't until Sept. 1, when the New Jersey Devils acquired winger Luke Evangelista from the Nashville Predators, that a trade involving an NHL player occurred.

That move could kick off another round of trades. Some teams could try to boost their rosters, while others could attempt to move players whose trade requests have yet to be honored.

Here's our take on five players who were fixtures in the offseason rumor mill and could be moved before training camps open.

It appeared Shane Wright's days with the Seattle Kraken were coming to a close this summer.

On July 5, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the 22-year-old center's agent claimed Kraken general manager Jason Botterill agreed to move his client to a team seeking a top young center.

The fourth-overall pick in the 2022 draft, Wright struggled to establish himself as a top-six center with the Kraken. On July 13, we published a list of five trade landing spots , including the Boston Bruins, Carolina Hurricanes, Montreal Canadiens, Philadelphia Flyers, and Vancouver Canucks.

Despite his difficulties, Wright still has plenty of potential. He had a solid rookie campaign in 2024-25, posting 19 goals and 44 points in 79 games, and could get back on track with a better club. He's in the final season of his entry-level contract , making him an affordable option for a cap-strapped club.

Of the clubs we mentioned earlier this summer, the Flyers and Canucks are potential destinations. They're young teams that could use depth at center and have the tradeable assets to pursue him. Perhaps the retooling Nashville Predators will also give him a look.

Carolina Hurricanes Trade Alexander Nikishin to the St. Louis Blues

Sitting at No. 4 on our August NHL Trade Targets Board , Alexander Nikishin seemed to be a prime offseason trade candidate.

The Carolina Hurricanes were reportedly considering whether to trade the 24-year-old restricted free-agent defenseman or re-sign him.

The St. Louis Blues were believed to be interested in Nikishin, who completed his entry-level contract last season and is ineligible to receive an offer sheet from a rival club. On Sept. 1, Jeremy Rutherford of The Athletic predicted the Blues would acquire the young blueliner from the Hurricanes.

Rutherford believes Nikishin is the type of big-bodied, left-shot defenseman that Alexander Steen, the Blues' new general manager, wants to add to his defense corps. He also predicted St. Louis could get him at a reasonable asking price and then sign him to a bridge contract.

If the Hurricanes peddle Nikishin, they could seek a good young player as part of the return, of whom the Blues have several.

It could give them an edge in any trade talks for Nikishin, provided they can get him inked to an affordable short-term deal.

Kirill Marchenko to the Montreal Canadiens

Trade speculation has dogged Kirill Marchenko since late June, following reports that the 25-year-old was unwilling to sign a contract extension with the Columbus Blue Jackets.

The winger held the No. 2 spot on our August Trade Targets list amid conjecture about potential landing spots .

The Montreal Canadiens were on our list of destinations following a report from Russia in July claiming the Blue Jackets were talking with other clubs about trading Marchenko. However, Columbus general manager Don Waddell swiftly refuted those rumors.

Waddell insists Marchenko will report to the Blue Jackets' training camp in mid-September. Nevertheless, James Murphy of The Sick Podcast cited a source claiming the Canadiens would be at the front of the line among potential suitors if the winger becomes available.

The Canadiens are seeking a top-six forward to play alongside budding superstar Ivan Demidov on their second line. Perhaps they could offer a trade package that includes defenseman Arber Xhekaj or winger Zachary Bolduc .

Several months have passed since Dylan Larkin's trade request was first reported. With the Detroit Red Wings searching for a new general manager, the 30-year-old center's situation remains in limbo.

Since June, Larkin has regularly appeared on our NHL Trade Target Big Boards . The Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, and Florida Panthers were on his initial three-team trade list, with the Dallas Stars rumored to also be among them.

The Wild were reportedly Larkin's preferred destination , but like the other clubs, they cannot afford the Red Wings' high asking price and his $8.7 million average annual value . That's unlikely to change regardless of who becomes the Red Wings' new GM.

If Larkin expands his trade list, it should increase his chances of being moved if the Wings have their new GM in place before training camp opens. That could be his only recourse if he truly wants to join a contender before the regular season begins.

Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck has sat atop our NHL Trade Targets Big Boards since July.

The three-time Vezina Trophy winner was reportedly close to being shipped to the Buffalo Sabres in late June, but the deal fell through before the opening round of the 2026 draft.

Hellebuyck became the focus of trade rumors after expressing his unhappiness with his performance and that of the Jets during his end-of-season media availability. On Aug. 27, he publicly revealed that he requested a trade in the spring, confirming what many observers had suspected for months.

Several teams could be strong landing spots for Hellebuyck, but the Sabres might still have the best chance of landing him. They possess considerable depth in young forwards and goaltenders to address the Jets' need for a top-six center or right wing, as well as a potential future replacement for Hellebuyck.

Our teammate Joe Yerdon believes the Jets would want a forward like Konsta Helenius, Noah Ostlund, or Zack Benson. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen could be a decent replacement for Hellebuyck on the Jets if they are not on his five-team no-trade list .

articles.title: Joan Mir defends himself over his crashes: "I know how to ride without crashing; it's very easy"
articles.summary: Mir says he has adopted a "never settle" approach as he explains why he crashes out so often from races
articles.body:
With 22 crashes last year and 16 so far this season, Joan Mir has suffered the joint-most falls of any rider on the MotoGP grid, but the Spaniard attributes his high crash count to the risks he has to take to extract the maximum performance from his Honda.

Marc Marquez left Honda at the end of 2023 because, among other reasons, he crashed off the bike every time he tried to make it go fast. That year, in 15 grands prix appearances, he suffered 29 crashes, almost two per weekend.

That same season, Mir joined the official team from Tokyo, and in the same number of grands prix, he crashed 24 times, exactly the same number of times he had crashed with Suzuki in total over the previous three years.

It's a dynamic that has accompanied him ever since.

In the 69 grands prix he has contested with Honda so far, Mir has recorded a total of 79 crashes, averaging more than one per event. Johann Zarco has posted similar numbers, crashing 49 times in the 48 grands prix he has competed in with LCR's RC213V, with the most recent in Barcelona leading to disastrous consequences.

At the Aragon GP, Mir was asked to interpret that statistic and the large number of crashes he was having, especially because most of those 16 crashes have been in races, and quite a few of them before completing the first lap.

"There is no specific explanation because every crash has a different reason," he explained. "At Silverstone, for example, I had contact at the start and crashed. What is clear is that if you start from the first or second row of the grid, you don't crash. The way of racing at the front of the races is very different from how you compete at the back. And what you have to try to do is be further forward.

"It is clear that we have had crashes of that kind, and also others from taking more risks than necessary and trying to push more than was possible. And these are the ones I have to control more as a rider."

This year, with 16 crashes each, Mir and Jorge Martin have fallen the most times so far.

"Many crashes come from trying to find more from the bike than there really is," he said. "I am an experienced rider, but now I am also a rider who has to take advantage of any opportunity to get a good result, because I don't know when another opportunity will come.

"Not having results consistently can have two readings: that it increases your hunger to do well, or that it switches you off for good.

"In my case, there was a moment in my career when I wasn't sure whether it was worth continuing. Now, on the other hand, if I have the opportunity, I try because I want to do it and I am hungry to achieve more. I should probably control that impulse because I don't have the bike to do more."

What draws the most attention about Mir's crashes is that his team-mate, Luca Marini , is the complete opposite. The Italian, in the 51 grands prix he has contested with Honda since arriving in 2024, has only crashed 13 times. Only three of those crashes came in races, two in his first season and just one in 2025 (Japan).

It's unclear whether Honda values the search for more performance, which inevitable leads to risks and crashes, or a measured approach in Sunday races.

"I think it is valued," Mir said. "In a competitive project, what is most appreciated is speed, trying to go to the maximum and getting the best possible result.

"Other types of projects may prefer development and finishing races. They are different ways of riding a bike. I also know how to ride the other way, without crashing.

"Surely, if you have the speed, going slower is very easy. But if you don't have it, going faster is the difficult thing. For me, the important thing is not to get used to going slower, but to push to always be a better rider. Never settle.

"That is the vision I have had at Honda, especially now. It is a very complicated situation to manage mentally for a rider who has won. That is the thing: when you have won and you know you can be at the front, you wonder why you are not there and you want to keep taking risks. But these are my demons."

While Mir previously admitted to having had "doubts about my future", he has now recovered his ambition, desire and excitement ahead of the 2027 season, where he will compete for Gresini on a satellite Ducati.

articles.title: Ben Simmons Gives the Kings a New Level of Lineup Flexibility
articles.summary: The Sacramento Kings are giving Ben Simmons a second chance to jump-start his career by signing him to a one-year contract after he was the number one overal...
articles.body:
The Sacramento Kings are giving Ben Simmons a second chance to jump-start his career by signing him to a one-year contract after he was the number one overall draft pick in 2016. Simmons missed the 2025-26 season due to injuries. However, he hopes to return and become the star he was early in his career. The Kings focus on Simmons as an experienced player they can use. His talent can be used in various ways, allowing the team to switch lineups and strategies during games.

Ben Simmons Gives the Kings a New Level of Lineup Flexibility

Standing 6-foot-10, Simmons has always been a unique player because he can play guard and defend multiple positions. He has averaged 13.1 points, 7.4 rebounds, 7.2 assists, and 1.5 steals in his career, along with being a three-time All-Star and earning two All-Defensive selections. His playmaking is one of his biggest strengths, especially in fast breaks, when he pushes the pace after a rebound.

On the other hand, it is hard to ignore Simmons' offensive deficiencies. He has not developed as a three-point shooter throughout his career. This makes it easy for defenders to leave him unguarded as they close down his teammates' driving lanes. He has also lost much of the scoring punch he had in his All-Star years, and injuries have sidelined him for significant stretches throughout his career. After missing the entire 2025-26 season, health will be a major concern for the organization as it navigates his time with the Kings.

Simmons could play many roles on the Kings' current roster, including alongside guards like Zach LaVine , Malik Monk , and rookie Darius Acuff Jr. , which gives the team plenty of players who can score on their own . This means Simmons will not have to be the primary scorer ; instead, he can use his passing to push the ball in transition and his size to create mismatches. Simmons can run ball screens with Acuff and make plays in the pocket toward the rim, or spray the ball to shooters. He can also be an extra ball-handler for the Kings and help them move away from depending on a single player to initiate every possession.

However, his defensive versatility might be even more valuable. Simmons can defend opposing point guards and switch to bigger players, giving the Kings a new option to handle different offensive styles. It would let him play alongside smaller guards and add size without taking the ball away from them. Finally, the Kings could use him alongside Sacramento's frontcourt players, including Domantas Sabonis , to build taller lineups.

In the end, Simmons does not need to recreate his All-Star form to contribute to the Kings. If he stays healthy, his passing, rebounding, defense, and fast-break ability could benefit Sacramento in different combinations. The team can call upon him as a reserve point guard, a point forward, or a defensive specialist depending on the needs of a specific lineup . Simmons' ability to influence the game without the ball could make him useful alongside other offensive players Sacramento already has.

Of course, the move raises concerns, especially about Simmons' shooting and injury history. However, Sacramento hasn't had this much versatility on its roster, and Simmons adds to the mix. If he remains healthy and takes the role of a complementary piece, Simmons can bring more options in terms of experimenting with the rotation and matchups. It is even more significant that Sacramento can use Simmons to show that he can still be an all-around player in the league.

articles.title: Man United fans urged to join major protest over ‘season ticket ban fiasco’
articles.summary: Manchester United fan group The 1958 plans to protest ahead of Sunday’s derby against Manchester City
articles.body:
Supporters of Manchester United are being urged to join together in a peaceful demonstration ahead of Sunday's derby against Manchester City, in response to what fan representatives have described as a "season ticket ban fiasco".

The club's summer crackdown on ticket touting has drawn widespread criticism, with supporters arguing that a heavy-handed approach has unfairly penalised innocent match-goers facing the threat of sanctions.

The supporter group known as The 1958 declared that a "line has been crossed", calling on fans to "stand united" outside Old Trafford prior to kick-off.

A spokesperson for the group stated: "Manchester United supporter groups are being called upon to all stand together following reports of bans and season ticket sanctions without clear and compelling evidence always being presented.

"For generations, match-going Reds have given their time, money and loyalty to Manchester United, home and away. That loyalty deserves to be treated with respect.

"This is not about one group or one individual. It is about how Manchester United treats its match-going supporters. It may not affect you today, it may not next time but that day is coming for all of us.

"All Reds. All groups. One voice. Show the evidence. Lift the bans."

Urging various fan factions to put aside past disagreements, The 1958 has asked supporters to assemble at 3pm on Sunday outside the Bishop Blaize pub near the ground.

Back in July, the group co-signed a joint statement condemning the club's measures, expressing a shared sentiment that it was a case of "ban first and ask questions later".

In August, Manchester United stated that an independent review of ticketing platform activity between March and June had "uncovered significant and organised touting". However, the club conceded that the investigation had "caused significant concern and distress for some supporters".

Addressing the fallout, the club said: "Manchester United accepts that the process may have caused distress for some loyal supporters, underestimated how common sharing account usernames and passwords was, and recognises that some fans may have felt they were being treated unfairly."

The first Manchester derby of the season is due to kick-off at 4.30pm on Sunday, with United currently five points behind their local rivals in the table.

articles.title: Why Wisconsin's Week 1 blowout loss wasn't as bad as it seems
articles.summary: The Wisconsin Badgers couldn't have asked for a much worse final score to open the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Wisconsin Badgers couldn't have asked for a much worse final score to open the 2026 season.

Wisconsin fell 41-13 to Notre Dame on Sunday night at Lambeau Field, but the 28-point margin doesn't tell the entire story.

In fact, there were plenty of reasons for optimism before things fell apart in the second half.

Wisconsin arguably looked like the better team in the first half

The best photos from Wisconsin vs. Notre Dame Shamrock Series

For the first 30 minutes, Wisconsin looked like it belonged on the field with one of the best teams in the country. The Badgers went into halftime trailing just 13-10 and did a good job limiting Notre Dame's offense. The defense kept the Irish from running away with the game, while the offense showed flashes of what it could become.

Quarterback Colton Joseph, making his Wisconsin debut, was particularly encouraging. He made several impressive throws down the field and finished 19-of-30 for 217 yards and a touchdown. His 28-yard touchdown pass to Malachi Coleman was one of the highlights of the night.

Obviously, the second half can't be ignored. Notre Dame scored 28 points after halftime, and Wisconsin struggled to generate much offensively.

Still, this wasn't a team that was completely outmatched from the opening kickoff. Wisconsin proved it could compete with Notre Dame for a half. Now, the challenge is figuring out how to do it for all four quarters.

articles.summary: Bijan Robinson could break Darren Sproles' all-purpose yards record in 2026
articles.body:
One thing above all else has become abundantly clear about the Atlanta Falcons going into the 2026 season: this is Bijan Robinson's team.

Usually that honor is reserved for whoever the starting quarterback is, but as the Falcons have no true QB1 on their roster at the moment, it falls to their best player and most-gifted athlete. Right now that's Bijan Robinson, and whoever is in second place isn't in the same stratosphere.

Robinson was just voted the third-best player in the entire NFL by his peers, and he's going to need a special season if the Falcons are going to continue their streak of seven-or-eight win seasons. How special?

According to Josh Kendall at The Athletic , not only can Robinson break Chris Johnson's scrimmage yard record, he can also beat Darren Sproles' record for all-purpose yards in a single season.

"Just predicting Robinson to break the yards-from-scrimmage mark wouldn't be all that bold. He came within 211 yards of Chris Johnson's record (2,509 yards in 2009) last year. To set the all-purpose mark (which includes return yards), he'll need to top Darren Sproles' 2,696 in 2011. This is not a bet that Robinson will return kicks for the Falcons this year. It's a bet he'll be overfed in both the rushing and passing scheme in Atlanta."

Even without returning kicks or punts Sproles' record should definitely be in reach for Robinson.

In fact, we think Robinson's ceiling is quite a bit higher, assuming he can stay healthy for the full season. If Robinson plays all 17 games and the quarterback room is as bad as it appears to be, it's possible that he could wind up approaching 3,000 total yards for the year.

articles.title: Patriots crack top five in AFC rankings ahead of 2026 season
articles.summary: Even with a tougher schedule, the Patriots are still viewed as one of the best teams in the AFC conference.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are approaching the 2026 NFL season with expectations to be one of the best teams in the AFC.

The Athletic ranked the Patriots No. 4 out of all 16 teams in the AFC for this season, determined by a panel of NFL executives, signaling strong confidence in New England's chances of having another successful season in 2026.

The ranking puts the Patriots just behind the Buffalo Bills (No. 1), Denver Broncos (No. 2) and Houston Texans (No. 3) in the AFC hierarchy. New England has assembled a roster capable of competing at the highest level against the best teams in the AFC, but the prowess at the top of the conference is strong heading into the season.

Much of the attention will center on the Patriots' ability to maintain their momentum throughout the season with a tougher schedule to deal with.

A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and Alijah Vera-Tucker will be expected to take the Patriots over the top in the Super Bowl race, while the Patriots' coaching staff faces the task of drawing up schemes to give New England an edge over the toughest teams in their way.

With Week 1 of the upcoming season on the horizon, another layer of anticipation around New England and its championship aspirations will follow the team into the upcoming year.
