articles.title: Jon Sumrall demands sharper defense as Florida turns to Campbell
articles.summary: Jon Sumrall reviewed Florida's win over FAU, detailed the corrections his defense needs and previewed the Week 2 matchup with Campbell.
articles.body:
Florida football coach Jon Sumrall reviewed the season opener against FAU and turned the page to Campbell and Week 2 in his weekly press conference on Monday.

Sumrall revisited Florida's season-opening win over FAU after reviewing the film, highlighting Aaron Philo's decision-making, the offense's perimeter blocking and Jadan Baugh's physical running style. He also addressed the defensive mistakes and lack of situational awareness that frustrated him Saturday night.

The Gators' coach provided several injury updates, discussed Florida's aggressive fourth-down approach and explained why Campbell presents a much different challenge than it did last season.

Appreciate y'all being here. I want to start by putting our thoughts and prayers with a good friend of mine, Mike Detillier, a longtime guy who covered sports in the state of Louisiana and worked with Bobby. I did Tulane Tuesdays for a couple of years with Mike and Bobby.

Mike passed really quickly after a couple-week battle with pancreatic cancer and a late diagnosis. He was always good to me. Thoughts and prayers to all the people around him and his family. It's a sad deal.

I'm excited to get back to work and practice today. We had about an hour, a little over an hour, of run-through. There is plenty to clean up from Saturday night's performance. There was some good in there, and there was a lot to correct.

Injury-wise, I would say right now Eric Singleton is highly questionable for this week. Emmanuel is also highly questionable. They have very similar injuries.

They're not out today. They're out at practice some, but not able to participate. We probably won't know their real availability until the middle or later part of the week, but they're definitely not probable as of right now.

Chieca is doing more and more. We'll see what that means for this weekend, but he's back doing more. He's close.

What stood out after reviewing the defensive film?

The biggest thing was situational awareness and football IQ. If it's third-and-1, we can't play nine yards off at corner. That comes with teaching. I thought we were maybe past that, but we can't forget that all those little details matter.

I thought we played hard when I watched it. It wasn't like the guys didn't give good effort. But, as a whole, it was awareness of play sequencing, tempo, how to handle tempo, how to communicate when we're facing tempo, when to challenge, when to play off and when to disguise certain coverage looks. There's a give and take.

Going into the game plan, the two big tasks defensively were managing their tempo and limiting their explosive plays because that's what they were good at. I don't think we managed the tempo well at times. We did limit the explosive plays. They really only had two, by how we count them.

Some of that limiting of explosive plays was because we were playing a little too cautiously and passively by not getting sticky enough at times.

I don't think it was an intent issue. It wasn't an effort issue. It wasn't a desire issue. It was simply that we're young or, in my opinion, untrained in certain spots at certain times. We have to coach better. Our players have to prepare in a manner where they can activate it on the grass on game day.

It wasn't all bad, but it damn sure wasn't all good either. There is a ton of growth that needs to happen within our football team.

At times, they had a good call against something we had going. Hats off to them. I really think that quarterback is a good football player. He creates, extends, has good pocket awareness and delivers the ball on time. He's tough and a good runner.

On the one he scored on in the run game, they had a good call against the call we had. If we had known that was what they were going to do, we probably would have liked a different call. I put that call in. That wasn't Brad White. I was like, "Brad, let's do this right here," and then it hit. Don't put that on Brad. That one is on me.

How do you correct overconfidence without hurting the team's confidence?

I want to be careful here. I just think you have to show up with a chip on your shoulder every day. You can never assume anything. I don't care who you're playing. As soon as you get complacent or overconfident, this game will humble you really, really fast.

Our guys have to understand each and every day — and that's everybody in our building, me included — that every seven days you're either going to be promoted or exposed. You're going to get exposed if you are not ridiculously dialed in.

I don't think anybody believes he's the best player in the country yet. I just think maybe we were a little too relaxed in our mindset and attention to detail at times. It could be how to play a certain call, down-and-distance awareness or what the offensive split and spacing are telling me.

When they got into condensed sets, we knew there were going to be stick routes. There were a couple of times when they ran stick routes, and we were nowhere to be seen near the receiver. There are other times when you give some of that stuff up. There is a give and take. You can't take everything away.

But we have to understand when to play more connected and attached in coverage. Our guys are going to improve. I promise you that. They're either going to improve, or I'm going to lose my mind trying to help them.

What is the value of playing a program from a lower level?

When I was at San Diego, we were non-scholarship. They still are. We beat scholarship teams. We beat Northern Colorado and Cal Poly, and we beat a lot of people who had 63 scholarships. We had none. Everybody was a walk-on.

Football players are football players. I don't look at one team and say, "Well, they've got this or they've got that." You have to earn it.

I think those opportunities are good for everybody, but I have a lot of respect for Campbell. I coached against Campbell, and they kicked my butt one time. I think it was 2010. They ran the option up and down the field on me. I've been to Buies Creek and gotten my butt kicked.

Why didn't Florida produce more pressure and sacks against FAU?

That's a good question. It was a combination of things. At times, they were getting the ball out quickly. At times, we didn't get off a block. Sometimes the quarterback extended plays with his feet. Sometimes we just didn't finish. We were really, really close and didn't finish.

We had several opportunities and didn't quite get it done the way we needed to. We've got to continue working on that. I thought we could have strained a little bit harder in certain scenarios. Each play was a little unique, but there was a combination of things that created the lack of sack production.

We were close to creating several more and didn't quite finish at the top of the pocket.

Which position groups stood out after you watched the film?

I was really fired up about our perimeter blocking. I wouldn't say that was just the receivers. It was the receivers and tight ends. On one of the perimeter run plays, you saw Amir Jackson, Bailey Stockton and VB in there. You saw some guys getting after people in the run game on the perimeter. That fired me up.

When your receivers and tight ends block like that, it usually promotes good football and a good running game. I was pleased with that.

I thought our offensive line played solidly. I wouldn't say they've arrived or that we're elite, but it looked like a well-coached, cohesive unit that played trained.

I thought our inside linebackers played solidly. I expect that from them, but they didn't play poorly by any stretch of the imagination.

I thought D.J. Coleman and Bryce Thornton both played pretty well. Anytime you're new and everybody is new with each other, there are a lot of unknowns. I thought all those groups played well.

The running back room also showed its depth. Obviously, No. 13 did what he does. Duke did some nice things. I think London Montgomery is a good football player, and B-Lou did some good things. Pryor was available and played a couple of snaps but didn't play many. He didn't feel like he could give it a full go. He should be back this week, but I don't know. We'll see how he responds.

How did Aaron Philo perform after reviewing the film?

I thought he made really good decisions with the football. The interception was not on him. That ball was very catchable and should have been a completion. He operated at a high level, communicated with confidence at the line of scrimmage and led.

I thought he knew when to tuck it and go a couple of times. Obviously, he scored on the one fourth down. On the other one, we were in third-and-long, and he scrambled to get it to fourth-and-inches or fourth-and-1. We snuck it on fourth down at midfield.

I thought he made good decisions for the most part. He wasn't perfect, but he played clean football and operated at a high level. The ball came out a little funky once or twice on shorter throws. I thought he threw the downfield balls really well.

The go ball to TJ was a really good throw. The one to Dallas on the comeback to our sideline early in the game was a nice throw. I thought he made some really quality throws and good decisions with the football.

How does Florida's offense put defenders in conflict?

What we do offensively and what our scheme presents is it threatens every area of the grass, vertically and horizontally. There could be a run play to one side and a pass play to the other. Which one do you want to defend? Defend them both.

There is a lot to manage for a defensive play caller and a lot of eye-violation issues that can be created when you're a second- or third-level defender. They put you in conflict a lot. It puts a lot of stress on the defense, and we have to continue doing that.

What did you think of the late goal-line stand?

I was pleased. I don't ever want to let anybody score. I wasn't pleased that they got down there the way they did. But our guys rose up and didn't just look at the scoreboard and say, "If they score this touchdown, we're still going to win."

They said, "No, we're not going to let them in."

It was a great play by Brendan Bett down there to fight, get off the block, tear off and make the play. I appreciate that they continued to play.

What caused Harrison Moore's snapping problems?

He had five bad snaps. Four of the five were on the same exact type of block. When you're playing center, you have to snap the football. That's important. But then you also have to block after you snap it.

We looked at the plays where he had the issue, and four of the five involved the exact same block. I'll say this for Harrison: He takes a lot of pride in his work. I would be out here during the summer at 4 in the afternoon. I'd walk onto my balcony to take a phone call or something and look out, and he would be out there with T.J. Shanahan doing extra snaps.

Most of the time, he was doing them while working on pass sets. Four of his five bad snaps came on back blocks in the run game. I said, "Hey, you probably need to start taking extra snaps while working on back blocks, not pass sets."

Trust me, we're very aware of that. I was pissed off. So was Buster. So was Phil multiple times. We'll get it cleaned up. Harrison takes a lot of pride in his craft and will get that corrected.

Did you enjoy not having to use the punter?

I did. I would love never to punt. I love Alec Clark. He's a great holder. He might be as good of a holder as he is a punter, and he's a pretty good punter. But, yeah, I don't care if I ever see him play.

Now, we may have to get his scholarship and NIL money back if he doesn't play. No (laughs). He's a good player, and we're going to need him. But it's fun not to have to punt. That's enjoyable. That's a fun night.

How clean was the offensive line's performance?

We had a false start, and the snaps weren't great at times. Those were the five snaps we talked about. For the most part, I thought we looked organized, prepared and targeted things well. There wasn't a whole lot of, "Why is that guy going the wrong way?" It was pretty clean.

There were a couple of times when it was, "You have to protect inside leverage here, and you got beat inside. You've got to do a better job." There may have been some hand-placement issues. But, for the most part, we functioned like a competent football team on the line.

It wasn't elite by any stretch of the imagination. It was competent football. We've got to continue getting better.

How did Florida's offensive tackles grade out?

I thought they played pretty well. I don't have the exact grades in front of me, but they played well. What we do helps them. We're going to run the football, put the ball on the perimeter and use play-action.

We're not going to put them in 50 drop-back passes a game where guys can tee off. I thought Buster called the game in a way that managed what they have to do well for them. But they're getting better. They're all getting better.

I thought Bryce played well. I thought Emeka played well. That was Dice's first game action here. He went in at left tackle, and I thought he played pretty well. That was exciting to see.

Who makes Florida's fourth-down decisions?

I make the decision about whether we go for it. I don't let somebody else make those calls.

We use analytics. John Donovan is on our staff. He's a former coordinator in college football and the NFL and a really good football coach. John helps me with all our in-game situational analytics. He's on the headset and will say, "Coach, it says fourth-and-7 to go here."

I'm like, "All right, we're going to go for it. Fourth-and-4, not fourth-and-7." I make the decision. We use the book everybody uses, but I don't just go by the book. I use some instinct, too.

I like to be aggressive. I think if you coach with an aggressive mindset, your guys will play with that mindset over time. If you coach passively, they're going to play passively. We're going to be fairly aggressive and calculating with our fourth-down opportunities.

Once we're outside our own 40-yard line, if it's fourth-and-1 and you're going to place a bet, you should probably bet on Florida going for it a lot. A lot of times, it's about the matchup. How is the other team's offense playing? What's the risk? How is our defense playing? There are a lot of things that go into it, but we're going to be confident.

Those are things we discuss well before Saturday. I looked at the analytics and the matchup all week. Sometimes you take the weather into account. You take your kicking game and their kicking game into account.

John helps with the decision. Buster is also informed before each drive about my thought process, and I make sure he's comfortable with that so he knows how to call third downs.

If I tell him, "Hey, on fourth-and-2, it's a go here," then being in third-and-4 gives him different options for calling certain types of plays. We try to sequence our plays well ahead of schedule so the guys understand how we want to play that drive.

Sometimes I'll tell him on first down, "Hey, if you get it to fourth-and-3 here, it's a go. Run it on third down."

Were you planning to kick a field goal before the fourth-down touchdown?

I told Buster, "Can we get seven or eight yards here to kick a more manageable field goal?" I'm glad Durkin made a 53-yarder, but I'd like to see if he can make a 40-yarder or a 35-yarder. Then, when he busted that run and we got to the 3-yard line, I'm like, "All right, let's go."

I had made up my mind that, if we got inside the 5 on that play, we were going to go for it. But I didn't think we were going to get inside the 5 because I was hoping to get enough back to kick a more manageable field goal.

Do you enjoy the game-management aspect of coaching?

I love it. I absolutely love it. What makes it fun is that you have to think fast, make quick decisions and be confident in those decisions. You can't second-guess yourself.

They're not always going to go right. I'll probably go for it on fourth down at some point this year and not get it. That's life. To me, that's part of what makes the game fun. You have to be prepared to make quick, calculated decisions that put your team in a position to be successful.

What are the injury updates on the other unavailable players?

Eagan (Boyer) should be back this week. He was at practice today and active. I think tomorrow is going to be full-go, but I'll check with Paul. I'll know today at 2:30 when I meet with Paul again about all our injury-report stuff.

Davian (Groce), I think, will be down for at least another week. It's nothing major, just a little bit of a back strain.

How did Kanye Clark perform while playing 72 snaps?

He did some really nice things. They did a nice job on the slot fade toward the south end zone and our sideline. On the other one going the other way, he got a little grabby, and they made a good throw and catch.

I thought he was active and leveraged the football pretty well. It's knowing whether I'm supposed to be outside of No. 2 or inside of No. 2 on certain box calls or in the screen game because they were a pretty good perimeter-screen team coming into the game.

We're probably going to roll some guys in there a little bit more to spell him. I thought I might have overplayed him from a snap-count standpoint. Alfonzo Allen, Lagonza Hayward and D.J. Coleman can all play down there. We need to build a little more depth and game experience there this week.

What stands out about Campbell's offense?

I'll tell you what, we haven't talked enough about them. We've talked a lot about our game last week. I have a lot of respect for this football team. They're well coached and have improved a ton from last year.

After watching their first game and then the second tape we got yesterday afternoon, I told our staff we shouldn't even watch last year's film. It's a waste of time. They're a totally different football team. They're averaging more than 500 yards a game right now. The quarterback is playing at a really high level. They've got really quality football players, and it's a challenge.

They didn't have the year they wanted last year from a record standpoint. But you can already tell there has been a shift within their football team in how they're playing. It has happened quickly from Year 1 to Year 2 with that coaching staff. We have a lot of respect for who they are and what they're doing.

How do you keep the team from looking ahead to Ole Miss?

That's so far away. That's so far away from me. I want to get better this week against Campbell, and then I hope that will help us later in the year.

I watched the game. Ole Miss is really good. I got my ass beat by Ole Miss twice last year. The ball comes out quickly from the quarterback. He has a really good arm, and they're a good football team.

But we've got to improve this week and focus on the theme for our football team: Be where your feet are. Be present all day Monday. I told our guys, "You want to be a pro football player? Raise your hand." Everybody says he wants to be one. Well, you don't have school today because it's Labor Day, so come back and do extra football work on your own if you want to be great.

We only get our four hours, but if you really care about being great, we've got a lot of work to do. I watched Ole Miss. They're really good. Everybody in our league is really good. Every time you strap up in the SEC, you know what you're going to get.

What challenge does Campbell's up-tempo offense present?

I've coached against Matt Kubik a couple of times. I believe the last time was when he was at Louisiana-Monroe and I was the head coach at Troy. I have a lot of respect for him. I love that you looked up who their offensive coordinator was. Matt is a really good football coach and presents a lot of challenges.

He does some really good things. They're going to stress us with some rules this week. They always do. It's another good test of how to get lined up, how to leverage the football from a perimeter standpoint and how to stay on top.

It's going to force us to communicate and take a step forward with situational awareness. That could mean down and distance, formation, split, spacing, the backfield set or where the tight end is aligned. All those things matter.

The biggest improvement we have to make defensively, like I said earlier, is not about whether our guys played hard. I've watched the tape a couple of times, and I think they care and play hard. I don't know that we played with great awareness or attention to detail.

At times, there is also a difference between playing hard and straining. You can play hard and give great effort, but straining to me is going two steps past that. We've got to go those extra steps. Matt and their offense will stress and challenge us. They do some good things, so we have to be prepared.

What stands out about Jadan Baugh when watching him at field level?

He is a powerful, sudden, violent runner who can stick his foot in the ground. The most impressive part of his long run to me was at the end, when he stopped on a dime and made two guys miss.

Then there was the downfield blocking. Go back and watch that play. Watch VB and Bailey Stockton, and then watch Luke Harpring come from 40 yards away to get downfield and try to help block. That was really fun.

Jadan is a good football player. He catches the ball well, even though he didn't have any catches the other night. That wasn't by design. We're going to throw him the football some. He runs with such conviction. You feel his runs. He's a violent runner who has gotten even better at running north and south.

When I got here and watched the tape, the one thing I talked to him about improving was that I thought he became a little too much of a cutter at times. It was like, "Dude, you're a big, physical man. Go that way, and you're going to be hard to deal with."

I think he has become more decisive. Make one cut and go. I'm really, really glad he's on our football team. I told him before the game Saturday night, "Thank you for staying here." I shared that with y'all after the game. I'm very glad he's still a Florida Gator. He's fun to watch play, and I'm glad he's on our football team.

articles.title: NY Giants must prove they belong in the fight up front with Cowboys
articles.summary: With John Harbaugh leading the way, Giants must refuse to let opponents force their will upon them, especially up front. That will be key to success.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD - The New York Giants have been pushed around for too long on both sides of the ball.

John Harbaugh wants to build a bully in the swamps of Jersey, and that's been the mission from jump.

The Eagles , the Cowboys and even the Commanders the last two years have all taken turns pushing the Giants around, mocking their existence regardless of the four Vince Lombardi trophies that sit in the lobby of their training facility.

It's time for the Harbaugh Giants to answer back. They need to squash the outside perception around the team that a while ago became a pushover in the NFC East and beyond.

The Giants have emphasized building a team that refuses to get dictated to between the lines, in back page headlines and on banners pulled by planes over MetLife Stadium like there were two seasons ago. You're not going to see any of that with Harbaugh here, at least not for a while, as his presence immediately raises the floor of the franchise.

That was going to take making over a locker room that needed to not only help establish a shift in expectations and results, but also do what is needed to change perspective and performance.

We have talked about creating identity, and for years - during the recent decade-plus of despair in particular - the Giants were quick to try and steal that from their past, instead of coming up with a new way of defining themselves.

There must be a refusal to let opponents force their will upon the Giants, which has happened far too often.

Truth be told: Harbaugh demands it. And if the Giants want to win and change their fate, they'll have to win physically up front on both sides of the ball, especially against the two teams that have dominated them in that regard for far too long.

That challenge begins with Dallas on Sunday night, and the Cowboys suffered a potentially significant loss when it was announced Monday that All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith will undergo surgery that will keep him out 4-6 weeks.

Smith's absense is enormous for Dallas, which already has questions at both tackle spots on the offensive line.

For the first time in a long while, the Giants have reason to believe they belong in that fight in the trenches.

But the toughness needs to come from the players, and it's not solely about want-to. Some players are just made that way, and in order to compete with the Eagles and the Cowboys, the Giants are not going to measure up consistently until they could match that edge not only with talent, but in their hearts and minds.

These Giants want to play with attitude, which they have this summer. They want to hit you and hit you hard, and if they take a punch, be resilient enough to hit back just as hard, even harder.

For years, the Eagles have been that way, and it's shown up on the scoreboard and in the standings - especially against the Giants, who have not won in Philadelphia since 2013. The Cowboys have done that, too.

If the Giants are going to compete at that level, they must alter the mindset and the football from the inside out.

Take a look at the offensive line. The Giants signed left guard Jon Runyan Jr. to a two-year contract extension, which means four of the five starting offensive linemen are now under contract through 2028. That's how the Eagles and Cowboys built their dominant groups, keeping units together with a mix of top shelf talent, draft picks and solid veterans.

Left tackle Andrew Thomas is in that first group, right guard Sisi Mauigoa is the prized rookie, and both Runyan and right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor represent the latter. Center John Michael Schmitz still has much to show entering the final season of his rookie deal.

The Giants now have three young, drafted offensive line that they believe in and not just for this year: Mauigoa, Marcus Mbow and J.C. Davis. Let them develop behind the starting OL, creating a strength with this group.

Eventually, they all could find different homes on the line. Don't move 'em in-season, though.

The Giants' pass rush of Brian Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux is incredibly gifted, and their production should be among the league's best. The inside linebacker tandem of Tremaine Edmunds and Arvell Reese has reshaped the way this defense will be viewed because of their uncanny skill sets in the middle.

What will decide everything is the play up front, specifically against the run. You know what you are going to get from veterans D.J. Reader at the nose and Shelby Harris beside him, but what about the snaps when they are not on the field? No one expects Reader and Harris to play 100 percent of the snaps.

The Giants will mix and match around them.

A trade for 370-pound beast C.J. Okoye from the Ravens. Veteran Dean Lowry plans to sign to the practice squad. They drafted Bobby Jamison-Travis and he has a chance to earn a role. Outside linebacker Chauncey Golston has been emerging as a 5-technique option.

There is more work to be done, but on paper, the run defense should be improved, especially from a schematic and communication standpoint.

How important of a factor was this in the Giants' quest to set a new tone under Harbaugh? Harbaugh left no doubt as far as the significance of not allowing opponents to impose their will on the ground back at the Scouting Combine in late February just weeks after he accepted the job.

"Well, we better [be improved] - it's a must thing, I can tell you that," Harbaugh said. "There's a lot to it. There's three levels and layers to your defense, and all three layers and levels have got to be committed to and incorporated in stopping the run, no doubt. Every single one of the 11 guys has got to be committed to stopping the run. You can't let people run all over you, there's no doubt about it."

articles.title: FSU football's winners and losers from ACC opening loss
articles.summary: Florida State forced four turnovers but could not capitalize enough in a 27-24 loss to SMU. See the winners and losers from the game.
articles.body:
Florida State had every opportunity to steal a marquee ACC win Monday night. The SMU Mustangs refused to let the Seminoles finish the job .

The No. 19 Mustangs overcame four turnovers, including two interceptions from quarterback Kevin Jennings and a muffed punt that Florida State recovered deep in SMU territory, to escape Doak Campbell Stadium with a 27-24 victory on Nick Reed's 20-yard field goal with 21 seconds remaining. FSU forced two fumbles and two interceptions, yet turned those four takeaways into only seven points.

Here are the biggest winners and losers from Florida State's ACC-opening loss.

Kromah continues to look like the centerpiece of Florida State's offense.

The sophomore followed his 115-yard performance against New Mexico State by setting a new career high with 116 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries. His 54-yard run in the second quarter set up a field goal, while his six-yard touchdown in the third tied the game at 17. Kromah became the first FSU player with consecutive 100-yard rushing games since Trey Benson in 2022.

Two interceptions cannot erase 430 passing yards allowed and several busted coverages.

Jennings consistently found explosive plays against the Seminoles, including touchdown passes of 50 and 79 yards. SMU finished with four receivers over 70 yards and averaged 8.7 yards per offensive play despite turning the ball over four times.

Winner: Florida State's ability to create turnovers

FSU's defense had plenty of problems, but generating takeaways was not one of them.

Quindarrius Jones forced and recovered a fumble on SMU's opening possession, Nehemiah Chandler intercepted Jennings in the end zone, Gemari Sands recovered a muffed punt and Ashlynd Barker added another fourth-quarter interception. Four takeaways should normally be enough to put a team in position to win.

The frustrating part for Florida State was what happened afterward.

One problem from the New Mexico State game followed Florida State directly into Week 1.

The Seminoles finished an ugly 2-for-15 on third down, repeatedly forcing their defense back onto the field and failing to capitalize on SMU mistakes. The contrast was significant, with the Mustangs converting 8 of 14 third downs.

FSU had four extra possessions created by turnovers and still managed only 324 total yards.

The contrast between these programs has become increasingly difficult to ignore.

Entering Monday night, SMU was 14-2 in ACC regular-season play since joining the conference in 2024, while Florida State was 3-13 over that same two-season span. The Mustangs' victory moved those records to 15-2 for SMU and 3-14 for FSU since the start of 2024.

The loss also dropped Norvell to 22-27 in ACC play during his Florida State tenure and marked FSU's third consecutive loss in a conference opener.

articles.title: “A struggle”: Paul Scholes says Carrick has a massive Matheus Cunha headache brewing
articles.summary: 1 Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has warned Michael Carrick that he may have a major problem on his hands with Matheus Cunha.StrugglingSeveral United...
articles.body:
Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has warned Michael Carrick that he may have a major problem on his hands with Matheus Cunha.

Several United players underperformed in Sunday's stalemate with Everton, but Cunha was the worst of the lot.

From overhit passes and heavy touches to poor positional awareness and glaring misses, his performance was a catalogue of errors. There was simply too much that went wrong.

In yet another game, Cunha didn't appear to have a clear role in the team. Last term, Carrick primarily used him on the left of the attack. But Marcus Rashford's return has seen him pushed elsewhere in the team.

Carrick appears to favour Rashford out wide, meaning Cunha has been deployed up front, in something of a false nine role, although sometimes Bruno Fernandes has assumed that role, with Cunha dropping into the 10.

The Brazilian has somewhat looked lost and lacking the inspiration and confidence he was oozing in his maiden campaign at Old Trafford. It's still early stages and he may still be getting up to full fitness but Scholes thinks Carrick has a dilemma on his hands.

The former England international said on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast , "It's very difficult to watch a Man United team without a centre forward."

"Now, what Cunha is, I don't really know what Cunha is, what is he a number 10 or a wide player."

"But he's definitely not a number nine. And watching the United team without a number nine, it's a struggle."

When Benjamin Sesko was introduced at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he looked much better and found the back of the net to temporarily restore United's lead.

The Slovenian rose highest to head home a superb cross from Luke Shaw before Ainsley Maitland-Niles broke the hearts of the travelling supporters with a stoppage-time stunner.

It will be interesting to see Carrick's selection when United face Sabah in their Champions League opener on Thursday.

articles.title: Lyon’s sporting director reveals why they chose Openda over Benzema
articles.summary: Karim Benzema is a free agent after his Al Hilal contract was terminated, and he wanted one last opportunity in European football by returning to his former...
articles.body:
Karim Benzema is a free agent after his Al Hilal contract was terminated, and he wanted one last opportunity in European football by returning to his former club, Lyon.

The Ligue 1 side were looking for a striker after Endrick returned to Real Madrid following his loan spell at the club, and signing Benzema made sense given his experience. Benzema also wanted the move to happen and was prepared for a return, but Lyon ultimately chose a different option.

Lyon signed Lois Openda on loan from Juventus , and Benzema never returned to the club. The French side were more than happy to land Openda and will hope he performs well for them, while Juve will also want him to succeed so they can either sign him permanently or have the opportunity to sell him.

Benzema's return to Europe was also complicated by clauses in his Saudi Pro League contract, which tie him to some off-field work in the country beyond his playing spell there. Those contractual obligations contributed to the difficulties surrounding a potential return to Lyon.

(Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Lyon sporting director Matthieu Louis Jean has now spoken about the two deals and explained why Benzema did not return, as quoted by Calciomercato :

"It's almost a fantasy. There was contact with an intermediary this summer. It didn't go any further: it was impossible due to contractual issues."

He added: "We didn't go any further because we needed a fast attacker and we were working on Openda."

Lyon therefore decided to focus their efforts on Openda rather than pursue a return for Benzema. Although the experienced striker was interested in rejoining his former club, contractual complications prevented the move from progressing.

For Benzema, the situation means his hoped for return to European football with Lyon did not materialise. For the French side, meanwhile, Openda became their preferred solution in attack, with the club now hoping the Juventus loanee can deliver enough quality to justify a potential permanent deal.

articles.title: Red Bull pull off crazy F1 stunt as Sebastian Vettel’s title-winning car takes to Madrid train tracks ahead of Spanish Grand Prix
articles.summary: International Sports News: Red Bull Racing have once again pushed the limits with a wild Formula One stunt. The team has put Sebastian Vettel’s championship-winning RB8 car on M.
articles.body: Red Bull Racing have once again pushed the limits with a wild Formula One stunt. The team has put Sebastian Vettel’s championship-winning RB8 car on Madrid’s train tracks ahead of the Spanish Grand Prix.The stunning project gave Madrid an early taste of F1 action. The car was converted into a bespoke train and taken onto the city’s Metro tracks. Former F1 driver Patrick Friesacher was behind the wheel for the unusual run.Red Bull Racing turn Sebastian Vettel’s RB8 into a train for unique stunt in Madrid Red Bull Racing teamed up with the Canillejas workshop to create one of the most unusual F1 demonstrations ever seen. The team took Sebastian Vettel’s RB8, the car that helped the German win the 2012 world championship, and gave it a major makeover.Engineers and mechanics fitted the F1 car with specially designed metal wheels. Each wheel weighed 29.8kg. That is around twice the weight of a standard Formula One wheel.The work was completed in record time. The finished car was then ready to run on Madrid’s Metro railway tracks. Former F1 driver Patrick Friesacher was chosen to drive the unique machine.The Austrian took the converted F1 car through parts of Madrid’s Metro network. The stunt included runs past Estadio Metropolitano station and the Sacedal and Chamartín depots.It marked a first-of-its-kind experience for the Red Bull Heritage team. Friesacher, who raced for Minardi in Formula One in 2005, admitted that the experience was unlike anything he had done before.“It was an unbelievable experience. I’ve been lucky enough to experience a lot with our Heritage team, but driving an F1 car on railway tracks was surreal. It’s very cool to add Metro driver to the resume”, he said in the viral video.The spectacular stunt comes ahead of the Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit.The event will be a major moment for Madrid. F1 is returning to the Spanish capital for the first time in 45 years. The last F1 race in Madrid took place in 1981. It was held at the 2.06-mile Jarama circuit.Ferrari driver Gilles Villeneuve won that race. Jacques Laffite finished second, while McLaren’s John Watson completed the podium.Nigel Mansell also competed and finished sixth. Keke Rosberg finished 12th, while Nelson Piquet and Alain Prost both failed to finish.Red Bull will now hope its fortunes change when F1 arrives in Madrid.Max Verstappen finished on the podium at last weekend’s Italian Grand Prix. However, the four-time world champion is still searching for his first victory of the 2026 season.Mercedes have dominated much of the campaign. Kimi Antonelli currently leads the driver’s championship.The Spanish Grand Prix 2026 will therefore be another major test for Max Verstappen and Red Bull Racing as they look to fight back. articles.title: Former Gunner has contract terminated by Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: Edu Gaspar’s contract with Nottingham Forest has finally been terminated, six months after the decision was made to part ways with the former Arsenal man.Pho...
articles.body:
Edu Gaspar's contract with Nottingham Forest has finally been terminated, six months after the decision was made to part ways with the former Arsenal man.

Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

Paul Taylor reported for The Athletic on Monday night that Edu Gaspar has officially left Nottingham Forest , with sources close to the club claiming the former Gunner's contract has been terminated.

Edu was working for Forest as their global head of football, but he didn't last long in the position. He was only officially appointed in July 2025, and by March 2026, reports suggested an internal decision had been made to part ways.

It took a long time for those reports to come to fruition, and The Athletic claim there's no expectation Forest will ever announce the departure in an official statement. But he's already been replaced via internal promotions.

Tom Hamilton reports for ESPN that Edu didn't play an active role in Forest's summer transfer window, which is unsurprising considering reports in March suggested he'd been told to stay away from the club and the training ground. Officially, Edu's last day in his role was last week.

Edu had initially signed a five-year deal with Forest, but the club held doubts about the director's long-term future following his clash with manager Nuno Espirito Santo last year.

Despite Nuno's departure, Edu's presence at the club remained a contentious issue behind the scenes.

Edu pushed for the signings of Douglas Luiz and former Gunner Omari Hutchinson last year, whilst Nuno and the recruitment team wanted other players. Luiz left the club in January, and Hutchinson is currently out on loan.

Edu was also key in the loan signing of Oleksandr Zinchenko from Arsenal , which did not go well at all. Zinchenko didn't even finish the season before leaving for Ajax .

Forest had a poor season, finishing 16th, and Edu appears to have taken a lot of the blame for that. This contract termination has been an inevitability for a long time now.

articles.title: Liverpool now considering deal for African star
articles.summary: This summer, it felt like Liverpool were being linked with a new player almost every day. The Anfield outfit had a lot of changes that needed to be made to t...
articles.body:
This summer, it felt like Liverpool were being linked with a new player almost every day.

The Anfield outfit had a lot of changes that needed to be made to their ranks and, while some were made, it still feels like they're a bit behind their title rivals.

For example, both Manchester City and Chelsea spent an absolute fortune on new players this summer and, while Liverpool may have splashed around £123 million on Bradley Barcola , his arrival was nothing in comparison.

Obviously, thanks to Barcola's arrival, on paper, Liverpool now have one of the best attacks in the world.

However, since Mohamed Salah is gone and the Reds still haven't replaced him with a natural right-winger, there's still a high chance that another attacker could be brought in over the next year or so.

So, the fact that the Reds are keeping their door open to new arrivals makes a lot of sense.

Liverpool could try and make another move for Ismaila Sarr in January

Throughout the summer, Liverpool's main goal seemed to be strengthening their attack.

Many different attackers were linked but, in the end, only two were signed.

Most people thought that an entire rebuild of Liverpool's attack was on the cards but, since they don't have an endless bucket of money to spend, that was far from the case.

So, even though the Reds' main focus was on improving their forward line, it now seems like their January transfer window could also be focused on bringing another attacker or two in.

That is, if a report from Football Insider is to be believed.

"Liverpool will consider making another move to sign Ismaila Sarr in January after failing to agree a deal before the summer deadline, sources have told Football Insider," they shared.

"Sarr was a target for the Reds throughout the transfer window after impressing for Crystal Palace over the last few seasons.

"Andoni Iraola wanted to add quality and depth to his attacking ranks following Mo Salah's departure.

"Bradley Barcola arrived in a move worth £120million before the deadline, and they remained hot on the trail of Sarr but failed to get a deal done.

"Sarr still wants to join Liverpool and he will stay on their radar in the months to come."

Liverpool must make sure they get a good deal for Ismaila Sarr if they sign him

Obviously, Sarr has plenty of Premier League experience and, since that's one of the main things that Liverpool are missing at the moment, a move for the Senegal international makes a lot of sense.

But, since he's 28 years old and has never scored more than nine Premier League goals in a season before, the £70 million + that Crystal Palace were demanding for him this summer felt rather steep.

However, if Liverpool really do want to sign the winger and do end up trying to get a deal for him over the line in summer, they must ensure that they get value for their money.

A fee around £50 million would be much more reasonable but, because of how big Liverpool are as a club and how desperately they need a right-winger, any attacker that they try and sign is going to be extortionately priced.

So, the best thing for them to do is just to see how things pan out and then re-evaluate in January, otherwise, they could end up making a deal that they end up regretting in six months and, since the Reds have already spent so much money over the last couple of transfer windows, that would be far from ideal.

articles.title: What the Patriots jersey you wear says about you in 2026
articles.summary: A rundown of some of the most common Patriots jerseys out in the wild, and what it says about the fan who chose to buy it.
articles.body:
For football fans, a team jersey is more than just a piece of clothing. It's a personality test that reveals a lot about the wearer as a person.

For New England Patriots fans, the choice of which player's jersey is worth spending upwards of $200 on is a big one. Typically, it reflects what kind of fan that person is.

So here's a rundown of some of the most common Patriots jerseys out in the wild, and what it says about the fan who chose to buy it.

Drake Maye, No. 10 — Have you said out loud that you love Drake Maye more than you've said it about your loved ones? The fact that you have to stop and think about it is troubling.

Mac Jones, No. 10 — You're weighing the pros and cons of being someone who covers up the name with duct tape.

Bailey Zappe, No. 4 — You held out hope deep into 2023 that Zappe was actually the guy.

Christian Gonzalez, No. 0 — You'd like to politely tell the Patriots to "JUST PAY THE MAN."

Ty Law, No. 24 — You'd like to tell the Patriots that you agree with the fan in the Gonzo jersey.

TreVeyon Henderson, No. 32 — You're worried about Rhamondre Stevenson stealing carries and diminishing Henderson's fantasy value.

Hunter Henry, No. 85 — Every time the offense gets to the 10-yard line, you say, "Here comes the play action."

Julian Edelman, No. 11 — You also own at least one of the following jerseys: Brad Marchand, Dustin Pedroia, Rajon Rondo.

Stefon Diggs, No. 8 — In the past year, you learned more about Cardi B than you ever expected to.

Antonio Brown, No. 17 — You refuse to admit this was a bad purchase and now use it to get a rise out of people at parties.

David Andrews, No. 60 — So, what brand of truck do you drive?

Tom Brady, No. 12 — When someone orders a bunch of pizzas, you're the one who will order a cheese pizza, even when others say it's "boring." You smile to yourself when the cheese pizza is the first one that's eaten.

One of those off-brand Tom Brady jerseys that's, like, black or camo — You scoffed at ordering the cheese pizza. But now that it's here, you're absolutely grabbing two slices.

Tedy Bruschi, No. 54 — You went to training camp this year and thought to yourself, "Practices are so soft these days."

Mike Vrabel, No. 50 — You used to have a great, underrated jersey. Now you just get a lot of bad Dianna Russini jokes.

Randy Moss, No. 18 — You've been waiting for this team to trade for a top-tier receiver for years and were ecstatic when they landed A.J. Brown.

A.J. Brown, No. 1 — You're really hoping this purchase doesn't turn out like your Stefon Diggs or Antonio Brown jerseys.

Rob Gronkowski, No. 87 — You've been politely asked to leave after you Gronk-spiked something that isn't a football at a public gathering.

Steve Grogan, No. 14 — People think the Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks was bad? You're ready to educate them about the '85 Bears.

Drew Bledsoe, No. 11 — You think fans in the luxury boxes are wimps who could never last 30 seconds on the cold metal bleachers at the old Foxboro Stadium.

Matthew Judon, No. 9 — There was a period of time where you thought he was the best pass rusher on the planet and should have gotten a bajillion dollars.

Matthew Slater, No. 18 — You clap politely for opposing teams instead of booing. It's just good sportsmanship.

Rhamondre Stevenson, No. 38 — You're constantly defending Stevenson as a lead running back and reminding people how good he was in 2022.

Troy Brown, No. 80 — You have rewatched at least one of the 2001-2004 Super Bowls at some point this year.

Devin McCourty, No. 32 — You were the one person at the bar actually watching the second half of the preseason game on the TVs.

John Hannah, No. 73 — You're overcome with an indescribable sense of despair when you have to tell other Patriots fans whose jersey you're wearing.

Tommy DeVito, No. 16 — You know all the best Italian restaurants in a 10-mile radius of your house.

articles.title: Baker relishing role in Walker Cup victory
articles.summary: Eliot Baker says helping Great Britain and Ireland win the Walker Cup still has not sunk in.
articles.body:
Eliot Baker says helping Great Britain and Ireland win the Walker Cup still has not sunk in.

The 23-year-old from Devon helped his side produce the biggest comeback in Walker Cup history to defeat the United States 13½-12½.

Baker beat experienced United States player Stewart Hagestad on the final hole of his singles match as GB&I overturned a three-point deficit going into the final individual round.

"I was in a complete state of shock for about 20 minutes until we actually lifted the trophy," he told BBC South West.

"It still kind of felt like the trophy was going to be going to them. I think just deep down it was almost what was expected with the scoreline going into the final session.

"But I'm sure over the next couple of days it will truly sink in."

The victory was Baker's only win of the competition, having halved the opening morning's foursomes and losing in the second morning's foursomes 3&2 with team-mate Stuart Grehan, but it proved to be vital.

"That is the highlight of my career, for sure," he added.

"Winning - that feeling was unbelievable. It'll take a long time to come down from that, but that is the pinnacle of amateur golf so it takes a lot to beat it."

Baker's win came in his second appearance at the Walker Cup, but it is likely to be his last.

He is planning on taking up golf full-time, meaning he will no longer be eligible for the amateur competition.

"I should hopefully be turning pro fairly soon," he said.

"As long as all things go well over the next month or so I should be turning pro and hopefully heading out on to the DP World Tour.

"But it's a little bit of a waiting game to see, but everything's in a good position so far."

A lot of fans are posting online that Lawson needs to make changes to the lineup, which comes with the territory. And with France coming up next, after hitting a record 22 threes against Nigeria, they could be right.

However, as great a player as Clark is, there are likely other reasons why Gray is playing. Two we can think of quickly are defense and quickness.

articles.title: Trevor Story’s Blunt Message Helps Jarren Duran End Negative Spiral
articles.summary: Trevor Story challenged Jarren Duran to end his negative self-talk before the Red Sox outfielder delivered a two-hit performance against the Angels.
articles.body:
Jarren Duran changed his appearance before changing the direction of his September. The Boston Red Sox outfielder cut his signature long hair during the team's weekend series in Baltimore, dyed it blond and then delivered one of his best offensive performances in months.

Duran went 2-for-4 with a home run and a double in Boston's 5-2 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Monday at Fenway Park. His solo shot was his 20th home run of the season and helped the Red Sox extend their winning streak to five games.

The new look created plenty of attention. A direct message from Trevor Story might have been considerably more important.

Trevor Story Challenges Duran's Negative Self-Talk

Duran has openly acknowledged his frustration throughout a season that has not always matched his expectations. Story, whose locker has been located next to Duran's for years, eventually decided his teammate needed to hear a difficult truth.

"He finally heard it enough in Baltimore," Duran said. "He's like, 'Dude, that's enough. All this negative self-talk, you're just making it a reality instead of if I talk positive, then positive outcomes will come.'"

Isiah Kiner-Falefa delivered a similar message.

Rather than allowing Duran to remain consumed by his season-long numbers, Kiner-Falefa encouraged him to focus on getting hot for Boston's postseason push.

That shift in perspective appeared to help Monday.

Duran homered in the second inning and added a double in the fifth, recording multiple extra-base hits in the same game for the first time since May 20.

That honesty has followed Duran throughout his Red Sox career. His intensity can help make him an electrifying player, but it also can turn every difficult at-bat into something larger than one out. Story recognized that pattern and challenged him to interrupt it.

Red Sox Need Duran Focused On September Opportunity

Duran's 2026 season has not completely followed the path he imagined, but it remains far from a failure. His 20th home run moved him within reach of a 20-home run, 20-stolen base season. Red Sox manager Chad Tracy also noted that Duran still has a legitimate opportunity to finish with more than 80 RBIs.

Those milestones would represent significant production, even if Duran believes he should have delivered more. Boston needs him thinking about what remains possible.

The Red Sox improved to 80-65 with Monday's victory and moved 15 games above .500 for the first time this season. They also remained within striking distance of the New York Yankees in the American League playoff race.

October could provide Duran with an opportunity to change the entire perception of his season. A productive postseason would matter considerably more than the frustrating stretches that preceded it. The Red Sox do not need Duran replaying every missed opportunity from April through August.

They need the aggressive, disruptive player capable of changing a game with his power and speed.

Duran's haircut gave his teammates something to joke about.

Story's message gave him something more valuable to consider.

The Red Sox veteran reminded Duran that repeating negative thoughts can turn frustration into a permanent expectation. Monday's performance showed what can happen when Duran gives himself permission to move forward. One strong game does not guarantee a September surge. It might be exactly where one begins.

articles.title: 'Pray': Arizona State HC Kenny Dillingham on facing QB Marcel Reed

Texas A&M and Arizona State University share a lot of mutual respect, with both teams speaking highly of each other ahead of their Week 2 matchup on Saturday.

After that quick joke, he went on to explain what makes Reed difficult to game plan for, and he put a lot of emphasis on how much more comfortable Reed looks in the pocket and how his touch on passes to all areas of the field has improved.

So, while certain people around and outside of Aggieland might not be as high on Reed as others, two of the top coaches in the country believe that Reed should get a little more credit for what he's been able to do up to this point.

Daniel Farke will take his side away from home on Wednesday evening, facing Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in Round Three of the EFL Cup.

The Whites have been a familiar opponent of the Blues in cup competitions over recent seasons, as well as the league, which have all been well-contested and hard fought encounters.

Speaking to the media ahead of Wednesday night's 8pm kick-off, the boss gave his thoughts on our latest encounter in West London.

He said: "We try to win it. That is a topic, the quickest way to Europe and to some glory.

"Of course, knowing that the Premier League always will have the priority and to make sure that we are as successful as possible there, and especially to reach our first goal, to establish ourselves on this level.

"We are not the favourites to win the EFL Cup. We know this also [will be a] challenging, difficult game. But of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid.

"At this stage of the campaign, of course, you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players.

"That is also important but, nevertheless, we want to be at our best and if possible we also want to go through into the next round."

Discussing the opposition, Farke added: "They have been stronger than they were last year. I judge more or less also like the offence, how they play with Pedro, with Palmer, with Rogers.

"There are not many teams in Europe who have such a quality. And also, if you look at the options on the bench, it is outstanding quality.

"So, they definitely have a top manager and also top players but we are looking at ourselves, and we also want to be competitive. We travel respectful but also not in fear. We want to go through into the next round."

articles.title: Why did Jeff Greenberg withdraw from the Detroit Red Wings’ general manager search this NHL offseason
articles.summary: NHL News: Jeff Greenberg has opted to remain with the Detroit Tigers, stepping away from the Detroit Red Wings GM search. Discover the impact of this decision on the Red Wings' crucial search for a new leader amid ongoing challenges.
articles.body: Detroit Tigers GM Jeff Greenberg has taken his name out of the running for the vacant Detroit Red Wings GM job and will stay with the Tigers. The decision removes a prominent cross-sport candidate from the running for Detroit’s NHL search, as the organization continues its search for a Steve Yzerman successor.Greenberg's decision comes at a crucial moment for the Red Wings, who are heading into another season without a playoff appearance. Add in a big leadership transition and trade request from captain Dylan Larkin, and the next hockey operations appointment becomes even more important for the franchise.Why did Jeff Greenberg leave Detroit Red Wings’ NHL search? The main reason is Greenberg's choice to remain loyal to the Detroit Tigers and to press on with the work that is already underway with the baseball organization. The Tigers said Greenberg told the Red Wings personally of his decision and thanked them for the opportunity.Greenberg had become an intriguing candidate, as his work had stretched across both baseball and hockey. He served as associate general manager with the Chicago Blackhawks for the 2022-23 season before joining the Tigers in 2023. That experience made him a viable option even though he is currently running an MLB organizationCommon ownership also strengthened the link between Greenberg and the Red Wings. It would be particularly interesting to see a move between two franchises of the Ilitch sports organization, as the Detroit Tigers and Detroit Red Wings are both owned by Ilitch. In the end, however, Greenberg decided to stick with the Tigers.How does Greenberg’s decision affect Detroit’s NHL search?Greenberg’s departure is one less experienced executive for the Red Wings to consider as the franchise searches for a new leader of hockey ops. Detroit is still trying to snap out of its long playoff drought after Steve Yzerman stepped down as general manager in July after seven seasons.The timing gives the decision extra significance. Detroit begins training camp with the organization still lacking a permanent general manager. The search is continuing with assistant general manager Shawn Horcoff running day-to-day hockey operations.The new executive will have some big decisions to make. Detroit missed the playoffs for the 10th consecutive season, finishing 41-31-10 for 92 points. One of the team’s most pressing priorities is roster management, as the team must also navigate how to deal with captain Dylan Larkin’s reported trade request.Greenberg’s departure, then, is about more than the loss of an unconventional candidate. It leaves the Detroit Red Wings to find another executive who can give a clear hockey operations strategy while working on roster construction, player development and the organization’s urgent push to contend for a playoff spot.Detroit moves on in the NHL search without one of the more talked-about candidates. articles.title: La cuenta pendiente de James Rodríguez para fichar por el Avellino y el factor Nesta
articles.standfirst: El sorprendente giro de James Rodríguez: negociaciones muy avanzadas para fichar por el equipo de la Serie B
articles.summary: El sorprendente giro de James Rodríguez: negociaciones muy avanzadas para fichar por el equipo de la Serie B
articles.body: El futuro del mediocampista colombiano James Rodríguez parece estar cerca de resolverse y dar un giro de tuerca tan sorprendente como atractivo. A sus 35 años y tras un periodo de incertidumbre que se extendió desde el cierre de su etapa en la MLS (donde militó en el Minnesota United) y su posterior participación con la Selección Colombia en la Copa del Mundo de 2026, el volante creativo se encamina de manera firme hacia el fútbol italiano. Según ha podido conocer MARCA, las negociaciones entre el entorno del jugador y el US Avellino —histórico club que compite en la Serie B de Italia— se encuentran en una fase muy avanzada, con un acuerdo que podría cerrarse en los próximos días. La noticia ha sacudido el mercado de fichajes, especialmente porque el nombre de James había sido vinculado de manera tímida con algunos clubes de primera línea o ligas exóticas tras la cita mundialista. Sin embargo, la oportunidad de recalar en el fútbol italiano cumple con una cuenta pendiente que el propio jugador había manifestado tiempo atrás en sus transmisiones digitales: jugar en la Serie A o en el Calcio italiano, una de las grandes ligas del viejo continente que le faltaba por tachar en su laureada trayectoria. A pesar de tratarse de un equipo de la segunda categoría, la ambición del proyecto del Avellino y el atractivo mediático de la operación han convencido al capitán de la tricolor. De concretarse, Italia se convertiría en el octavo país europeo en la carrera de James, sumándose a sus experiencias previas en Portugal (Porto), Francia (Mónaco), España (Real Madrid), Alemania (Bayern Múnich), Inglaterra (Everton), Grecia (Olympiacos) y Turquía. Uno de los grandes atractivos que seducen al volante colombiano para aceptar este desafío es la figura de su banquillo. El Avellino es dirigido actualmente por una leyenda viviente del fútbol mundial y campeón del mundo en 2006, Alessandro Nesta. El técnico italiano ve en James la pieza diferencial ideal para nutrir su medular, inyectar experiencia de máxima categoría y liderar el proyecto deportivo con el objetivo claro de pelear por el ansiado ascenso a la Serie A. Por su parte, la familia D'Agostino, propietaria de la institución italiana, ha asumido esta operación no solo desde una perspectiva estrictamente deportiva, sino como un movimiento estratégico de enorme impacto financiero y de marketing. La llegada de un referente mundial de la talla de James Rodríguez elevaría de manera exponencial la visibilidad internacional del club, atrayendo nuevos patrocinadores y situando al modesto equipo de la región de Campania en el centro de la escena mediática global. Para James Rodríguez, este movimiento representa un "rescate" competitivo crucial. Tras disputar el Mundial 2026 con el combinado cafetero —donde la selección firmó una actuación recordada hasta los octavos de final frente a Suiza—, el mediocampista acumulaba varias semanas como agente libre, a la espera de una propuesta que le garantizara protagonismo y continuidad. Su último encuentro oficial a nivel de clubes databa del pasado mes de mayo, cuando vistió la camiseta del Minnesota United. El Avellino, que ha tenido un arranque de temporada dinámico en la Serie B ubicándose en la parte alta de la tabla, busca dar el salto definitivo de calidad. Con la inminente incorporación de James, el conjunto campano se prepara para dar uno de los golpes maestros más sonados del mercado estival europeo, devolviendo al talentoso zurdo a los scudettos y canchas del viejo continente en busca de una nueva e ilusionante etapa dorada.

articles.title: From power failures to moral victories, Monday night couldn't have gone much worse for Florida State fans
articles.summary: Florida State's Labor Day loss to SMU stretched college football beyond Saturday, but the close score at Doak Campbell Stadium may save Mike Norvell.
articles.body: Week one of the college football season is always an absolute blast, mainly because instead of a lone Saturday of action, your weekend of football watching gets stretched to three magical days over the holiday weekend. One of the highlights of every week one is always the standalone game on Labor Day night, but unfortunately for Florida State fans, their Seminoles were the ones tasked with entertaining a football hungry public. The game itself was somewhat entertaining and had plenty of drama, but we will discuss that here in a bit. SEC TEAMS WENT 16-0 IN WEEK 1, IS THE CONFERENCE BACK ON TOP OF COLLEGE FOOTBALL WORLD? By now, everyone is aware of the power outage that took place at Doak Campbell Stadium on Monday night. If you were tuning in to watch Florida State take on SMU, you were likely greeted with a mostly dark stadium and a bunch of reporters sitting around a desk trying desperately to fill air time. MANY ARE MAKING THE ARGUMENT THAT JORDAN TRAVIS WAS THE GREATEST COLLEGE QB OF ALL TIME, AND THEY AREN'T WRONG The broadcast crew for ESPN did an admirable job with what they were given, but make no mistake about it, this was a national embarrassment for a program that has been full of them these past 24 months. Unfortunately, the power failure wasn't even the worst part of last night's "Debacle at Doak." FROM FSU TO DAN MULLEN, HERE ARE THREE 'OVERREACTIONS' FROM WEEK ZERO OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON Sure, it was fun for fans of every other team to sit back on their couches, pointing and laughing at FSU's incompetence with regard to paying their electric bill, but once the game started, it was a lot closer than anyone was willing to predict in the lead up. And a close game late into the fourth quarter is precisely what Noles fans DID NOT want to happen. To be clear, SMU dominated this game. The Mustangs marched the ball up and down the field seemingly at will, racking up nearly 600 yards of total offense and going 8-for-14 on third down, but it almost seemed like they were trying to give this game away to the Seminoles. WHICH HEAD COACH'S SEAT IS HOTTER HEADING INTO 2026 SEASON: SHANE BEAMER OR MIKE NORVELL? And FSU simply would not take it. A game in which SMU outgained Florida State by 261 yards came down to the final possession, which presents a nightmare scenario for any Seminole supporter looking to offload head coach Mike Norvell's albatross of a contract. The Noles are 1-1 and have a "competitive" game against a top-25 opponent under their belts, so anyone hoping for an exit strategy with their beleaguered head coach might be in for a rude awakening. It would have been better to get blown out on national television, especially with the pregame power outage. A close loss that came down to the last few seconds gives Norvell a sliver of hope, which as we all know is poison. Don't get me wrong, there were plenty of other embarrassing moments for the Noles that represented a microcosm of the Norvell era, like this joker who dribbled an imaginary basketball on third and ten right before his defense gave up a 30 yard completion. Seminole fans are in football purgatory right now. There doesn't seem to be an end in sight, and a close loss to a College Football Playoff hopeful was basically the equivalent to God adding another million tons of sand to their hourglass of suffering. The money will be raised to cut ties with Norvell eventually, but $51 million is a big chunk of change, and the powers that be will be looking for every reason not to pay it until that number comes down. If you're an FSU supporter, you should be praying that this season goes off the rails, because 7-5 with close losses to teams like SMU will only prolong the inevitable. articles.title: SEC threatens to boot LSU out of the conference this week, court filing says
articles.summary: The Southeastern Conference will meet on Thursday to determine whether to boot Louisiana State University out of the high-profile conference as the fight over the Tigers’ potential use of former professional football players escalates.
articles.body: The Southeastern Conference will meet on Thursday to determine whether to expel Louisiana State University out of the high-profile conference as the fight over the Tigers’ potential use of former professional football players escalates. In a federal court filing, the conference said it will meet to “decide whether to terminate Louisiana State University as an SEC member institution.” The filing represents a dramatic escalation in the showdown between the conference and one of its founding members. A back-and-forth legal battle over whether athletes who graduated high school in 2022 would be allowed a fifth year of eligibility has created chaos as schools and conferences deal with the fallout. Some state courts, including in Louisiana, paved the way for those athletes to play another year in college – and that opened the door for some athletes who had left school to pursue a professional career to return to the college game. While many schools have shied away from letting former pros play for their teams, the Tigers have decided to embrace the chaos. LSU and the SEC have been at odds over what the conference called a “deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes” to the school’s football team. The SEC has ruled it is against conference rules to have former professional players on the rosters of member universities’ teams. A Louisiana court ruled last week that the school could allow Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris to play on the Tigers’ football team despite both players having spent time in NFL training camps over the summer. Both players are now enrolled at LSU but head coach Lane Kiffin left them off his roster for Saturday’s blowout win over Clemson. In the filing, the SEC said it has “longstanding provisions that prohibit individuals who have entered a professional draft, signed professional contracts, or been rostered on a professional athletics team from returning to compete in college athletics (the “Professionalism Rules”). These rules are built upon an essential principle: college athletics are reserved for students who are actively pursuing an education while competing for their universities.” According to the filing, LSU has left two roster spots open for Wright and Harris and have “indicated their intent to place those athletes on LSU’s official football roster.” “Defendants have continued their public efforts to recruit professional athletes and eventually allow them to participate in official team activities in direct defiance of the Professionalism Rules,” the filing stated. “This conduct is detrimental to the Conference and contrary to its core purpose. Defendants’ conduct has already harmed the Conference and threatens to cause further substantial harm if not curbed.” In a statement, the SEC added it is asking the court for a temporary restraining order that would allow the conference to enforce its own rules after the Louisiana court blocked it from enforcing the rule against former professional players being available to play. “The SEC and its member universities have the right to establish, through agreed-upon governance procedures, the rules under which they voluntarily compete and to expect those rules to be followed. A commitment to those rules, and to the core principles of the Southeastern Conference, is an essential element of SEC membership,” the statement read. “Today’s filing is necessary to defend that right and preserve the Conference’s ability to govern competition among its members.” CNN has reached out to LSU for comment. This is a breaking story and will be updated.

articles.summary: Buccaneers name six captains for 2026 season
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will have a new-look leadership group in 2026, with players voting for six team captains ahead of Sunday's season opener against the Cincinnati Bengals . Quarterback Baker Mayfield, tackle Tristan Wirfs, wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr., nose tackle Vita Vea, linebacker Alex Anzalone and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. were selected by their teammates. Mayfield, Wirfs, Vea and Winfield return after serving as captains last season, while Godwin Jr and Anzalone join the group.

The changes come during an offseason in which Tampa Bay lost two players who had been fixtures among the team's captains. Lavonte David retired after spending 12 of his 14 seasons with the Buccaneers as a captain. Mike Evans, who left Tampa Bay for the San Francisco 49ers in free agency, had been selected as a captain in each of the previous nine seasons, but was not selected as a captain on his new team. Godwin Jr now steps into an even larger leadership role as one of the longest-tenured players remaining on the roster, and the veteran receiver previously served as a Buccaneers captain in 2023 and has spent his entire NFL career in Tampa Bay since being drafted in 2017. Anzalone's selection may be the most notable of the six, considering he only joined the Buccaneers in March. His teammates have already seen enough to give him the captain's patch. Anzalone isn't unfamiliar with the responsibility, either, serving as a captain in all five of his seasons with the Detroit Lions from 2021-25.

The other four selections provide some continuity. Vea will serve as a captain for the fifth consecutive season, the longest active streak on the team. Mayfield, Wirfs and Winfield will each enter their fourth straight season with the honor. Mayfield also previously served as a captain during stops with Cleveland and Carolina. Perhaps the biggest takeaway from the selections is how Tampa Bay's leadership core continues to evolve. David and Evans were two of the most recognizable voices in the locker room for more than a decade, leaving significant shoes to fill. With Tampa Bay preparing to begin another season with postseason expectations, those six will be the players their teammates look toward to help set the tone.

articles.title: Jacob Sexton injury update: Oklahoma State football OL out for season with leg injury
articles.summary: Oklahoma State football lineman Jacob Sexton injured his leg in Tulsa loss and will miss the rest of the season.
articles.body:
STILLWATER — Oklahoma State starting left tackle Jacob Sexton is out for the season with a lower right leg injury , coach Eric Morris said Tuesday.

OSU's depth chart entering Saturday's game against No. 2 Oregon (11 a.m., ESPN) lists junior Desmond Magiya or sophomore Shaun Torgeson at left tackle. Against Tulsa, Magiya was the first to replace Sexton at left tackle while Torgeson and senior Ashton Lepo took turns also.

Sexton, senior left tackle, injured his right leg on OSU's first offensive series of the season. Playing at Oklahoma last year, Sexton suffered a season-ending injury in the first game.

"Heart goes out to Jacob, a guy who has definitely been our best offensive lineman since we've been here," Morris said Saturday. "Somebody that's worked so hard this offseason to get himself back into shape. He's been plagued by injuries his whole entire career."

Morris said after the Tulsa game he will watch the film and grade his replacement options along the line.

"I didn't think we had a great answer on the edge," Morris said. "(Magiya) got beat a number of times around the edge, got a holding penalty at a crucial time in the game. So I think Sexton, obviously you lose a really good player at left tackle, that's not what you want but that's not an excuse. They took it to us in so many different areas."
